The objective of the mission is to facilitate social inclusion of DHH with disabilities. For that, the volunteer will be in charge to create and support living spaces ensuring local animations such as exhibitions, varnishing, etc.  
	IRSAM already has many works of art from years of creation and history of its residents.
	Our organisation would like to be able to showcase these creations through an art library (artothèque).
	The volunteer would have to launch and manage social inclusion projects or open mind activities like intercultural workshops, cooking workshops, sports events.
	IRSAM has received the quality label of the European solidarity corps. 
	This label allows it to host and send European young people with few opportunities to complete a several months mission into our institutes. 
	Irsam is in charge of European projects (HIPEN and ENVITER network) with other European partner institutions.

The volunteer will be accommodated in a private room on the top floor of the Chaumette building on the IES Les Primevères in Lyon. He will also have a shower (at the first floor) and toilet (on second floor). The volunteer will be provided with accommodation and food, and meals which can be taken at the workplace.

Training in french, and french sign language.

The profile of the volunteer should be comfortable with social interactions and have some experiences in the scope of disability and/or sensory impairment.
	As all our residents are deaf, the communication with the residents is in French sign language. A sensitivity to the world of deafness is a must.
	However, a basic training in LSF is possible.
	We would like to welcome a volunteer of Italian or Spanish nationality or speaking, with adaptability, entrepreneurial skills, comfortable and enjoyable artistic and/or sports topics.
	An understanding and/or speaking French is a plus.

Fantasia AG is a community of interest for cultural and integrative leisure activities for children, young people and adults. We stage plays, have our own band, tour all over the world and invite small and large artists of circus culture to our Zirkus Fantasia every summer. For some years now we have been running our own circus school, which regularly offers various courses in juggling, trapeze artistry, acrobatics and varieté for children & adults. In addition to our circus courses, we offer various leisure activities for adults with disabilities: a play group, coffee rounds, theatre and band projects.
Our two European volunteers support our trainers with school projects and afternoon classes. They are invited to contribute their own skills and ideas and, depending on their motivation and ability, also lead their own group. Our office team also welcomes their support in the areas of social media, project documentation, participant acquisition & event preparation as well as follow-up.

The volunteer will live in a spacious shared flat together with the second Circus volunteer. Those two will be the only permanent residents since the other residents just use their rooms infrequently. The building has recently been modernised and has a large common room that is a living room and kitchen in one. The volunteer rooms are equipped with a bed, desk, chair and wardrobe. The  bathroom is to be shared with the other volunteer. From the flat, it takes about 25-30 minutes to get to the city centre by bus or train, or faster by bike. To the beach it'll be 45 minutes with train.

Volunteers will participate in two mandatory seminars where they can connect with other European volunteers from other cities. They will also receive German language support for the initial period.

Being interested in working in a circus and with other people. Being cheery, open-minded and receptive to the unfamiliar. Due to the requirements of the daily work (guiding children in courses etc.), applicants with ADVANCED GERMAN LANGUAGE SKILLS are needed. All those interested please send your CV to zsombor.sonnevend@dug-mv.de.

LEAP Lestonnac is a vocational High School focused on People care and Services to territories professions. It's located in a rural environment and provides vocational training for youngsters aged between 13 and 20. We are looking for 1 volunteer to promote international mobility and interculturality! The volunteer will have to develop ways to interact with students during non-formal periods (such as breaks, meals, outings, evening time at our boarding school, etc.) to support the learning of the Spanish language not only inside but also more importantly outside of the classroom. He/She will also be able to develop personal projects related to the promotion of international mobility and interculturality, social and language exchange, etc. These are some of the activities in which the volunteer will support the team and share with the other volunteer on-site (International Civic Service).

The volunteer will live in front of the School in an apartment for 2 , including 2 private bedrooms, shared bathroom, a small kitchenette and a living-room. He/She will share it with the ISC volunteer. Free time can be spent in or off site. He/She will be off during the weekends and most of the school holidays (seminars organised by ESC will take place over holidays). All the meals will be provided and served in the school cafeteria (including weekends and holidays). There is access to all health or administrative services in the village and public transportation to visit other cities.

The volunteer will attend 2 seminars organised by the National Agency. The volunteer will mainly be guided to develop educational skills: professional practices, approaches in terms of formal and non-formal education to then integrate them into their professional career. They will be able to develop their oral and written communication skills, using all the resources at their disposal (including digital), before, during and after the mobility and the setting up of educational activities. They will learn or improve speaking and writing in French and English.

If you are interested in education, you want to know more about our Erasmus projects, and you are an outgoing person, this opportunity is for you. We are looking for 1 SPANISH SPEAKING volunteer who should be able to take initiative and communicate easily with students, eager to gain a new intercultural experience with a good capacity of adaptation. The volunteer should be outgoing, self-motivated and/or have experience in communication and international mobility. Some characteristics that will suit the profile: reliable, sociable, approachable, responsible, flexible, organized, creative, charismatic. The selection of candidates will be made by 3 people responsible of the school and the project.

We are a European network of civil society organisations, municipalities and research institutions dedicated to improving democracy through youth participation. We work with EU-funded projects related to youth participation, youth work and youth mobility. The selected volunteer will be involved in non-formal educational activities, support in managing social media and content creation, graphic design, photography, and video editing.

Regarding accommodation, we will rent an apartment for the volunteer, ensuring that he/she will have a single room (or a room shared with another person of the same gender) as well as a living room, a kitchen, and a bathroom. Project SOLARIC seeks 2 young people willing to spend 6 months volunteering while supporting families with children with special educational needs in Nansana, Uganda. The volunteers will be hosted by Uganda Pioneers Association and join the local teams working at two community centers - Centre for Special Abilities (CeSA) and Doreah Child Care Uganda (DCCU). Team SOLARIC wishes to contribute to a society in which children with special needs can grow and develop to their full potential for independent living. full_description:
Join us in Metz, France, to promote European citizenship, intercultural dialogue and youth engagement! As a volunteer, you’ll organize creative events like eloquence and writing contests, interactive stands at festivals, language cafés, and cultural workshops. You'll support youth exchanges and help create videos, podcasts, and social media content about European values and young voices. You’ll also be encouraged to develop your own initiative with the support of our team. This is a great opportunity to meet new people, learn about European programs, and contribute to building a more inclusive and democratic Europe.

Accommodation will be provided. The volunteer will receive a monthly bus ticket, as well as pocket money and food allowance.

During the volunteering period, the volunteer will participate in two national-level trainings: an on-arrival training and a mid-term reflection seminar. These sessions will help the volunteer engage with their experience, reflect on their progress, and develop new skills. Additionally, other training opportunities will be available to further support the volunteer’s learning and personal growth.

We’re looking for a motivated young person who is curious about European topics, enjoys working with others, and wants to make a difference. No specific diploma or experience is required. If you like organizing events, creating content (videos, articles, social media), exchanging ideas with other young people, or exploring different cultures, this mission is for you! An interest in citizenship, communication, or intercultural dialogue is a plus. You should be open-minded, creative, and ready to take initiative. Basic knowledge of French or English is useful but not mandatory, what matters most is your motivation and willingness to learn. This project is open to all young people aged 18–30 from EU and partner countries.

Pocket money 4 euros per day.

In the European Solidarity Corps (ESC) programme, travel costs for volunteers are reimbursed based on the distance between the volunteer's place of residence and the project location. The reimbursement follows the distance bands set by the European Commission and is calculated using the official ESC distance calculator.

Volunteers initially pay for their travel expenses and are reimbursed by the supporting or hosting organization upon presentation of valid travel documents (e.g. tickets, boarding passes, receipts).

On-Arrival Training
This training usually takes place within the first few weeks after the volunteer’s arrival in the host country. It is designed to help volunteers adapt to their new environment, understand the ESC programme and their rights and responsibilities, and get to know other volunteers. The training also includes cultural orientation, practical information, and support in setting personal learning goals (such as through the Youthpass process).
Mid-Term Training
This training takes place approximately halfway through the volunteering project, usually for projects lasting longer.

We are looking for a motivated and open-minded young person (18–30 years old) from Europe, interested in volunteering and eager to be involved in community activities. No specific experience or qualifications are required, but a positive attitude, willingness to learn, and respect for different cultures are essential.

The ideal candidate is flexible, proactive, enjoys working with people (including children, youth, or seniors), and is ready to contribute to a multicultural environment. Basic English skills are helpful for communication, but not mandatory.

Most importantly, we value enthusiasm and a genuine desire to make a difference!

Through “Youth for a Better Future,” we aim to foster social cohesion by promoting a sense of belonging within the local community and European space, advocating for equality among community members, and encouraging active participation in decision-making at all levels.
Volunteers will support the physical development of facilities of the future youth center “Horizons.” Their primary tasks will involve engaging in physical development and arrangement of the space, which includes assembling, organizing, and maintaining facilities, planting trees, arranging green spaces. 
Also, volunteers will participate in preparation of materials for thematic workshops, activities, events, supporting facilitators who coordinate youth activities and working with the local community.

Based on the ESC budget, each volunteer receives 120 Euros/month pocket money and a 150 Euros/month food and basic needs allowance. Volunteers will be accommodated in Targoviste area, in shared rooms (non-smokers rooms), with shared bathrooms and access to a common kitchen. The travel to Romania and back will be reimbursed based on the travel documents and program rules. Volunteers will be free during Spring (Easter) holiday and other legal days.

Volunteers will receive pre-departure training which will be provided by support and hosting organization. At the start of the volunteering program the training will be continued with thematic sessions carried out by volunteer coordinator. Also volunteers will be involved in an official On-Arrival training carried out by the Romanian National Agency for all international volunteers. The hosting organization will support volunteers with proper preparation to carry out the tasks, with mentoring and constant feedback. Lessons of local language will also be provided.

This volunteering position require interested persons in the field of active citizenship, community development and interested in youth activities. The volunteers must be open-minded, proactive, motivated to learn and develop personally and professionally, also to be sociable persons.
Volunteers must be open to move in a small city and support the host organization in its daily work with the local community. English skills, B2 – level is required, also willingness to learn Romanian language.
The project focuses on inclusion and will emphasize the participation of volunteers who face various socio-economic, geographical, cultural and other barriers.

Auxilium is a social enterprise created in 1984 in Altamura; a Type A cooperative which manages social healthcare services. Auxilium operates in the sector of psychiatric, disability, the elderly, schooling, training and volunteering. The volunteer will take part in the implementation of various rehabilitation activities carried out in 2 different structure, to support educators and users. The volunteer will be initially trained about a correct approach with people with disabilities, working methods, spaces, roles and rules within it. Finally, the volunteer, assisted by an educator, will be involved in the daily life of the Centres, in its relations with users and the realization of activities. The volunteer has to take part in all the activities and to learn from every sector of the structure that is provided for the users. After the first months the volunteer will choose the activities he/she wants to develop more or/and develop a personal project inside the structure

The volunteers will be hosted in a shared flats in center of Altamura. The flat have a kitchen, living room, shared sleeping rooms, shared bathroom. The apartment is shared with other ESC volunteers, everyone is responsible for taking care for the flat - cleaning, shopping and cooking. Each month every volunteer has the right to receive a the pocket money and money for food. There is no need for transport because the working and living place are at walking distance.
Read all details here: https://www.linkyouth.org/hosting/1065-coordinating-esc-project-in-altamura

Long-term volunteers will be followed during all the activities by a tutor who will favor their job placement and integration within the working group, thus favoring one full and active participation in all the activities of the NGO. The tutor will organize meetings programming periodicals in which the other members of the NGO will participate, and will be made available to contribute to the resolution of any voluntary need. In order to facilitate the integration of the volunteer not only in the organization, but also in the community local, a mentor will be identified.

The youth from 20 to 30 years is expected to be open minded, flexible, interested in the work with people who live fiscal or mental limits, open to learn techniques of management of a disabled person and will to support the qualified staff. Interest in Italian culture and language is important and readiness to learn in every moment of the project, experience in the field of disability is a plus point, but not obligatory.

Treasure Junior School was established in 2009 to support orphans in Uganda, many of whom lost their parents due to the Northern War and AIDS. The school, along with its kindergarten, serves 270 children aged 3-15. It is located in a densely populated suburb with poor living conditions and inadequate educational infrastructure, 6 km from Kampala. Description of tasks: 1) Support as a co-teacher in classroom, 2) Support in co-curricular and extracurricular activities (e.g., teaching creative subjects such as dance, music, art, drawing, or physical education), 3) Build the capacity of the team by enhancing pedagogical knowledge and skills, 4) Assist in computer training lessons for staff and learners, 5) Train staff and learners in basic digital competency skills, 6) Optional, depending on the volunteer's skills: Design a simple webpage for the school, establish social media platforms; train the staff on how to use them.

Accommodation will be provided in a shared apartment with other volunteers, each having their own lockable bedroom, located in the suburbs of Kampala. A monthly allowance will be provided to cover food, transport, and communication expenses. The volunteer will be responsible for preparing their own meals. Public transport in and around Kampala primarily consists of commuter taxis, known locally as Matatus. For shorter distances within the community, the volunteer will mainly use motorbikes called Boda Bodas.

The volunteer will participate in an online pre-departure training, followed by an in-person induction upon arrival at the host organization. Additionally, the volunteer will be encouraged and provided with financial support to learn the local language.

Previous experience working with children, even in informal settings, is desirable. While a background in teaching is beneficial, ability should be valued over formal qualifications. The most important attributes of a suitable volunteer are a love for children, creativity, friendliness, and a cheerful attitude.  The volunteer must be open-minded and emotionally resilient, with the ability to adapt to the local environment. The volunteer must be proficient in English.

🌟 Volunteer at EBEN EZER in Český Těšín!

Join EBEN EZER, a center supporting adults with mental and combined disabilities. Our mission is to provide long-term assistance that helps individuals develop work and social skills, boosting their independence and employability. 💛

As a volunteer, you’ll support workshops and therapeutic activities, get creative with knitting, crochet, sewing, ceramics, paper, cloth, and wood, and learn new skills while building meaningful connections. 🎨✂️

You’ll also accompany clients during leisure activities, sports, cultural events, and excursions, sharing experiences and making a real impact every day. 🌈

👉 Learn more: www.intervia.cz

💸 Volunteer with us – Costs Covered!

Thanks to the European Solidarity Corps, most of your expenses are sorted:

- Private bedroom in a shared flat 🛏️

- Food allowance: 4200 CZK (~170 EUR)/month 🍽️

- Pocket money: 7 EUR/day 💰

- Travel covered: Flights & daily commute ✈️🚗

- Only pay for your own free-time activities 🎨🎢

Focus on the adventure, the experience, and making a real difference! 🌟

🌟 Say YES to Volunteering with Slezská Diakonie! Join a vibrant group of international volunteers dedicated to bringing light to those in need. ✨ 
You will:
• Engage in meaningful activities and outreach programs 💛
• Impact the community 🌍
• Build unforgettable experiences and friendships 🤝
You’ll participate in training seminars to support your growth, guided by a coordinator and supervisor. Slezská Diakonie fosters a safe environment where every volunteer feels valued and part of something bigger. 
Step in, make a difference, and embrace the adventure — together as a community! 🌈

💫 Are You Ready to Volunteer at EBEN EZER?

If you’re between 18 and 30, open-hearted, eager to grow your professional skills, and excited to embrace new experiences, this project is made for you! 🌟

We’re looking for creative individuals who enjoy sharing ideas and have practical experience working with people, especially those with disabilities. A positive attitude and a smile are essential, along with proactivity and a willingness to learn Czech. 😊

Bring your energy, creativity, and compassion — and help make meaningful moments in the lives of adults with disabilities every day. 💛

👉 Learn more: www.intervia.cz

The AGSA  advocates for democratic coexistence and equal social participation, irrespective of  origin, religion, language, or other characteristics. Our activities are primarily focused on fostering intercultural openness in Saxony-Anhalt and supporting the development of international connections within our federal state on multiple levels.
To strengthen the implementation of green practices and raise awareness of sustainability, we are actively seeking a new volunteer!
Project Activities: 
-Development and implementation of green practices 
-contributing to our “SDG club”
-raising awareness towards sustainability (upcycling workshops etc.).
-Assisting long-term projects and organizing intercultural learning activities alongside fellow volunteers 
-participating in various local projects, such as the language café
-Preparation and organization of “ Eurocamp” (an international summer camp) and participating actively in the project as a teamer

You will share a flat with 2-3 ESC volunteers. Your living arrangement will include a private bedroom, a shared kitchen, and a shared bathroom. Free WI-FI will also be provided. At the beginning of each month, you will receive funds to cover your food expenses. The rate is determined by the National Agency and currently stands at €9.60 per day for food and €6 per day for pocket money. During training Seminars, you will recieve full catering instead of the food money. Local transportation is also covered.

During your ESC, you will be required to participate in two essential seminars: the On-Arrival Training and the Mid-Term Seminar. Additionally, there will be a monthly meeting where you will gather with all Magdeburg volunteers to discuss the current situation, collaborate on joint activities, or visit other projects. There will also be opportunities to engage in other seminars and workshops, with the condition that they do not conflict with your primary tasks and activities.

Very good proficiency in English.
strong command of the German language (good or very good).
Good proficiency in a further language is advantageous, preferably Russian, Ukrainian or Polish.
Keen interest in Sustainable Development Goals and education for sustainable development.
Ability to work effectively as part of a team while also being self-reliant and creative.

Forest Family Club Kaluzníček (www.kaluznicek.cz) was founded as one of the first outdoor nursery schools in the Czech Republic. It is located in the village of Lomnička, near the town of Tišnov. From Tišnov, there is a good train connection to Brno (27 km), the second largest city in the country.
Kaluzníček is a small nursery school with a maximum of 18 children (aged 3–7) per day and 2–3 pedagogical staff. We emphasize learning through natural experiences and plenty of outdoor activities. There is generous space for free play, creativity, and projects, both outdoors and indoors — the club operates in a yurt, beside a stream and forest.
Volunteers contribute by actively taking part in daily activities, sharing their passions, or simply spending time with the children. They can also join a wider community of families and volunteers connected to Kaluzníček and nearby alternative schools (Montessori, democratic, etc.).

The volunteer will have his/her own room in a well equiped house or flat in Tišnov and share common area (kitchen, bathrooms, living room and a garden) with another 4 volunteers or a flat with separate rooms. During the day there is a possibility of a healthy lunch. The volunteer will arrange his meal in the morning, in the evening and during weekends. The transport to/from Kaluznicek could be arranged by bus, bike or walking (2kms) or with parents driving their children. Volunteers get the pocket and food money monthly. There is a strong support from the community in material and social terms

As members of the Kaluzníček guide team, volunteers take part in guiding children through daily activities, supporting their development of empathy, cooperation, and conflict resolution. They help create a safe and inspiring atmosphere, assist in organizing celebrations and community events. The volunteer can also visit and experience other schools in the region/city - democratic school, Montessori school and Montessori forest kindergarten. The volunteer will be offered Czech lessons, ESC trainings, a lot of activities organized by volunteers (cooking, climbing, yoga, football, etc.). T

The volunteer can be any enthusiastic person, who wants to have experience in work with children and gain experience with alternative pedagogical methods as free play, democratic school, environmental education. The volunteer should have an appropriate physical condition (the forest club program involves outdoor physical activities during all seasons) and mental fitness (the children can be sometimes noisy and very active). Open-mindedness, playfulness and sense of humour are appreciated as well as a good level of spoken english. We do not require any specific education. In case there are more applicants with similar profile we prefer a person who can stay for a longer time, best option would be the whole year.

Voluntary Service of Armenia (HUJ) was founded in 1965 and is situated in the center of Yerevan. HUJ is a member of the Coordinating Committee of International Voluntary Service (CCIVS) at UNESCO and the Alliance of European Voluntary Service Organisations.
The volunteer will assist in HUJ activities and promotion of volunteering lifestyle, in organization of international voluntary activities, promotion of HUJ volunteering projects. 
The participant will learn the aspects of a work in a voluntary service organisation's office, how to organize international voluntary workcamps, seminars/trainings, details of a work with long-term volunteers. After finishing the project, HUJ will help the volunteer to find a job in a voluntary service organisation. 
The volunteer will also have Armenian language classes in a language center twice a week, located not far from the office of HUJ.
The volunteer will always find here a friendly atmosphere. 
Duration of the project is 8-12 months.

On the first of each month, volunteers receive a monthly allowance, sent by HUJ to their bank cards, covering their pocket money, food, transportation, and internet expenses.

Upon the volunteer's arrival at the airport, they will receive a warm welcome by HUJ. Following this, an introductory meeting will be held at the HUJ office, where the organizational staff will formally greet the volunteers and assist in essential procedures for their stay in Yerevan (obtaining an Armenian phone number, a physical bank card, and arranging a meeting with their assigned mentor). During their mobility in Yerevan, volunteers will engage in two training sessions - an on-arrival and a mid-term training - organized by SALTO in Georgia.

There are no gender restrictions regarding the selection/recruitment of volunteers. As per the ESC guide, the age of the volunteer should range from 18-30. The volunteer should be interested or have some experience in working with children; he/she should be enthusiastic, responsible, respectful, thoughtful and reliable. The main criterion for the choice of the volunteer-to-be are the activities they have planned for the project.

Les Courmettes is a natural site of 600ha in a Natura2000 area. Located nearby Nice, scientific studies and monitorings are implemented along side actions to raise awereness and train people. The volunteers, under the direction of the nature activities manager, will participate in protecting this rich site by reconciling both nature conservation and welcoming the public. They will take part in: 
- raising public awareness (through panels, discussion, educational tools) 
- species and habitats studies (fieldwork, data analysis)
- site management (trail marking, site defence etc.) 
- learning french (10% of the time), communicating about the ESC (through videos, stands, articles) (10%) 
- tasks related to the proper functioning of the Les Courmettes centre:  welcoming visitors, maintenance of the domain and its park, various tasks related to Community life (30%).

The volunteers are housed at the centre of Les Courmettes, which is also the logistic base for the projects, the head office and the hub for running the life of the team. They share rooms (1 to 2 people of the same sex per room). Lunch and supper are eaten together during the week with the team and any other participants at fixed times. They are prepared by a cook. The Rules of life might be adapted due to the COVID situation.

Training will be provided on arrival concerning the modus vivendi at the centre community life, week planning and project and activity description. Field work training is provided for the volunteer all through the project such as: species identification skills, protocols, use of observation tools and other field equipment. The St. Martin care home for old people is in the city of Löffingen. The supporter of this institution is the hospital charity foundation in Löffingen. This is a legally independent public charity; it is not for profit. The care and support of residents in the old-age care home St. Martin is organized by an all-inclusive (mind and body) programme. The newest knowledge is used in the areas of nursing care, medicine, and social aspects. Meeting the individual needs of the residents is a team effort. The residents, family members, doctors and the care specialists all work together. Basic care, treatment care, and social care are all focused on the resident. The nursing specialists work together with social care workers to help the residents. This makes all-inclusive care possible. The use of European Volunteers is mainly for the social care and daytime support of the residents. Volunteers can co-design the daily programme. They are supported by the nursing support staff.

Volunteers are given a single room in a shared flat together with other volunteers, trainees, interns etc. in a separate part of the nursing home.
Volunteers can take part in the communal catering in the house, for days off they receive a meal allowance or can come to the dining room for meals.
ESC volunteers receive a D-Ticket, which allows to travel easily and flexibly throughout Germany - whether by bus, train, tram or S-Bahn! It is valid for all public transport across the country.

To decrease problems from the start, volunteers go to important introduction seminars where they'll receive information about the institution and their duties.
There is continuous professional support for the volunteers. One example of support is regular reflection talks. A neutral person from outside of the core group will lead these talks.
Apart from the compulsory EVS training cycle provided by the National Agency there is also weekly language training at the local adult education center.

Desired profile of volunteers:
Our projects are outlined for young people with less opportunities in terms of education, therefore we don't accept graduates (Bachelor/Master) or students from university.
We prefer young people without university entrance qualification who might be interested to start a vocational training in Germany after the voluntary service.
Volunteers should be interested in working in the social and health care sector and be open to working with elderly and/or disabled people and people at risk of exclusion.
Volunteers should be able to develop and plan activities on their own initiative, but also be able to contribute innovatively and collaborate within the team.
A basic knowledge of German would be helpful and a willingness to learn German is expected.
A class B driver's license would be helpful.
 We expect a long term participation (min. 10 months) because the persons cared for in a nursing home need stable personal relationships, therefore it's not possible to change the volunteers frequently.

With our Hungarian partner, you will help homeless people and families in need, providing them with accommodation and helping them to increase their chances for reintegration with the help of social work and other services.

You will find there everything you might need during your stay. The place is in Budapest, about 30-40 minutes from the city center by public transportation.

With us, before departure:
- We make sure that you participate in a preparatory training day in the Netherlands (free of charge: we pay for your travel costs for this training).
- If you want, we can also help you write a convincing motivation letter and a good resume in English.

- As a volunteer, you will get mandatory training courses organized by the National Agency of your hosting country (on arrival and mid-term training).  
- Depending on the organization, you may also get extra trainings during your project.

Also you will be learning more about the processes behind the curtains of a German NGO on the topic of volunteering work. Our office is located in Berlin Weißensee at Antonplatz.

Furthermore, you are going to attend one or two (depending on availability) mandatory seminars in different German cities to reflect on their learning progress. The seminars are great opportunities to meet other volunteers from all around Europe working in Germany. A mentor will facilitate the learning process and support you with any upcoming challenges during the volunteering period at VJF. Project "Learning by to doing - Diaconal Year in Poland" is involving volunteers from different countries into structures of social/charity/educational institution. One of them is The Primary School in Konin. The pupils are 7 to 15 years old
The school helps students developing their interests in extra classes and interest circles: mathematics, languages, art, tourism and others. The most important aim of the school is to enable each student to become: successful learners who enjoy learning, make progress and achieve their aims. The volunteers will participate in organising activities for children in the day care room (educational
games, sport activities, activities related to music or theatre, depending on the volunteers interests and abilities), leading intercultural workshops and interests circles about volunteers native culture,tradition, language for pupils (in their free time- before or after regular lessons), helping the pupils with the homework, school trips.

The volunteer can cook for himself/herself or eat lunch at the hosting organisation canteen. The volunteer will leave near the School.

As our profile is ecology and health we prefer the volunteer who promotes a healthy life style.

We are focused on international and intercultural dimension of our organization in long-term, our team is international and consists from members of different backgrounds. Any other member from another country enriches the activities of the organization, bringing new activities and ideas to the preschool community. For the school year 2025/26 we have 4 spots for volunteers, acting as assistants in our 2 preschools Vyšehrad Monsters and Libeň Monsters and also in our afternoon English Club for school-aged kids. The travel will be covered by the organization on mutual agreement about the concrete travel dates and means. The public tratsport card in Prague will be provided.

The volunteer will be monitored and supported by professional teachers with long-term experience, thus the whole volunteering period will be an opportunity to gain experience in the field of preschool education. Any other trainings of volunteer's interest will be supported.

Volunteers should have an interest in working with preschool kids and good level of English as main language of program and communication with kids, parents and colleagues. Besides that, the talent and enthusiasm to do such activity is the only criteria. The volunteers may also act as individual assistants for kids with special needs, so experience with such assistance would be helpful. We prefer volunteers who would stay for the whole school year September-June.

The ESC HumAid Volunteering Program in Okhaldhunga, Nepal focuses on four development areas: Public Health and Wellbeing, Child Protection, Early Childhood Education, and Teacher Development. Volunteers support local communities by assisting health workers, promoting hygiene and sanitation awareness, organising creative learning activities for children, helping Early Childhood Development Centres, and participating in teacher training support. The goal is to empower marginalized communities and contribute to sustainable development.

Volunteers stay in the Naratika Community Learning Centre (VIN hostel) in Okhaldhunga. Accommodation is simple, with shared living spaces, separate rooms for male and female volunteers, bunk beds, basic kitchen access, shared bathrooms, and occasional power cuts. Basic Nepali food is provided; specific dietary requirements must be managed by volunteers. Laundry service is available for a small fee.
Volunteers spend the first night in Kathmandu, then travel by jeep to Okhaldhunga (approx. 8–9 hours). Project sites are reached by walking (10 minutes to 1–1.5 hours daily).

We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated volunteer ready to join our 180-day project in Nepal as soon as possible.
No formal physical fitness requirements, but volunteers should consider their limits, as daily walking to the work site is required. Volunteers should be open to simple living conditions, a rural environment, and working with marginalized communities.

Like hundreds of young people before you, who had a fantastic experience with our elderly, join our association to be part of this beautiful solidarity chain! By visiting them, forming friendships, engaging in intergenerationnal projects, introducing them to digital tools, proposing new social activities... We want to allow 2 young European to have a memorable and exciting experience of volunteering within a well-known organization where staff and volunteers work alongside! In France, we are already a solidarity chain of 15 000 volunteers and 600 staff! Location of accomodation and mission: La Seyne-sur-Mer, on the Mediterranean seaside, in a peaceful place called "La Villa des Fleurs". The project is operated by “Friedenshof Kommunität e.V.” - a non-profit association - with the vision to support the
international understanding, tolerance as well as international ethos based on the idea of non-violence. The association’s
main activities are taking place in and by the Friedenshof-Gemeinschaft, an intentional community of currently 11 adults and 2 children.
The aim of the project is to afford a young person to get to know alternative ways of life and work in an
international dimension as well as to discover various subjects like sustainability, community life, spirituality,
communication, economics and non-violence theoretically but particularly practically.
The volunteer will participate in the community life’s structure (3 daily rituals) and have various responsibilities. There are
routine work, tasks based on different community projects or seasons as well as the own projects of the volunteers. (garden, construction site, kitchen, sheep, fruit processing...)

The volunteer will stay in a single room in the old house or, if she prefers, in a caravan
on the community area. Kitchen and bathroom is shared with the community and
other guests.
Organic vegetarian food is provided; for lunch time, it is a common meal and for
breakfast, dinner and always in between, kitchen and food stock are open for selfservice.
Taking part in cleaning the kitchen after the meals is part of the normal daily
household routine for everyone.

The participant will take part at the On-arrival-training and the mid-term meeting, organised by the National Agency. There is also the possibility to take part in various seminars taking place at Friedenshof community.

The “Friedenshof Kommunität e.V.” likes to welcome one volunteer for one year. The person may have social, geographical or economical obstacles.
The participants want to live in a rural environment and spend a lot of time outdoors in the garden, with the animals and on the premises for various activities. 
In addition, they would like to get to know community life as alternative to usual forms of living and look forward to intensive contact with the other community members.
You are interested in a sustainable lifestyle, where consumption and expensive leisure activities step back.

WE ArtCoop is a Humanitarian Aid ESC project that involves a total of 15 young people from European countries in the development of a participatory project to raise awareness and empower women and children in Shianda (Kenya) that live in a vulnerable situation due to gender-based violence and its consequences. For 6 months, 6 volunteers will join and support WEFOCO team in creating new spaces for women and children, promoting active participation and involvement of the target group in their empowerment process, and promoting critical conscientiousness in each context through awareness actions. Volunteers will design and develop innovative non-formal education and artistic methodologies to raise awareness in different social problems detected on their context (gender-based violence, sexual education/health and mental health) in which working mental health, consequences of gender-based violence and the importance of sexual education that they will carry out during the whole project.

Volunteers will receive 600€ per month as financial support. In addition to this, they will be accommodated at WEFOCO’s facilities, which are specifically prepared for youth volunteers working with the organization. Volunteers will stay at the same location throughout the entire volunteering period, with accommodation arranged from their very first day. **Visa, travel, and insurance support** are also included for the duration of their volunteering.

Participatory observation during the analysis phase of the project by volunteers and workers from WEFOCO. Creation of promotion group with all the agents of the project and community, to plan together the program and the activities. Develop different artistic awareness and training activities on WEFOCO’s day-to-day program. Regular activities with the community, and the support and follow-up by tutors. Common evaluation through promoting group, of the activities developed.

Volunteers have to be interested on developing artistic and community skills, working with excluded communities to empower their identity. It is valued to have knowledge in socio-educational field and non-formal education skills. It is also important to have a vocation on social themes. It is valued the participation in social projects with excluded communities, youth and population. It is important for the youth to have interests related to exclusion, woman rights vulneration and motivation to learn about social realities and community art methodologies to work on empowerment.

Your daily work will be to prepare and realize workshops in schools and youth organisations about European Union, different languages and cultures from primary school to high school. You will also be able to promote environnement, digital transition, fight against discrimination, democracy by creating workshops..Furthermore you'll be an ambassador of the EU Solidarity Corps (presenting the programme to young people). In addition to this you will be presenting further programs to stay abroad (Erasmus +, DFJW/OFAJ...). You will be an ambassador of Europe and international mobility. Every year we celebrate the Europe Day, Christmas in Europe and further events (debates, conferences, webinars). You will be working together with the team to develop those events and European projects.You will also work on communication tasks (social networks, website)... Furthermore, you will be asked to create your own animations and activities about your country and your culture.

You will receive pocket and food money at the beginning of each month. Accomodation will be in a youth dormitory called Habitat Jeunes Laval. You will be hosted in a fully equiped appartment with 1 other European volunteer. You will have you own room. You have the possibility to cook in your appartment or to eat in the canteen of Habitat Jeunes. Every evening Habitat Jeunes dormitory offers animations for the inhabitants (sport evenings, cultural evening, games etc..) Transportation from home country to Laval and return will be paid up to 275€ or 360€ depending on the distance.

National Agency in France proposes an arrival training in South of France with other volunteers and a mid-term training. At your arrival, you will get a training with the House of Europe and 3 other volunteers to get all the necessary information to put in place animations about Europe and you will have a tutor to guide you through your project.

More information here : https://maison-europe-mayenne.eu/we-are-looking-for-volunteers-2/

- Interest in animation and in working with children - Convinced in the European Union project and interest about EU news - Interest in promoting EU, interculturality, diversity - Interest in promoting European priorities like : environnement, digital transition, fight against discrimination - Team work - Open-minded and curious - French beginner - Motivated to work in a multicultural environment

We are searching for a volunteer who is passionate about sustainable development and environmental issues. The volunteering includes youth work at the youth centers, community work, gardening and working actions and mantaining outdoor green area (LivadaLAB), events with exchange of second hand clothes. The volunteer also has to have interest in technical tasks, co-creating community and ecological/environmental activities. Some tasks are: events that address sustainability and healthy lifestyle (funky fleat market, second hand events, picnics, star gazing, seed exchanges, workout...); giving ecological inputs in Zavod Bob’s activities; attending team meetings; idea implementation; facilitating DIY, sports, cultural, and repair activities (natural materials, bikes,  cooking...); supercycling (T-shirts, bags...); managing second hand clothing (including IG “fashion show stories)...

As a part of the volunteering project we will provide you with a fully equipt rented apartment. You will have a private room in a shared apartment with 3 other volunteers from different countries. Apartment is 3,2 km away from the youth center and close to shops, restaurants, farmacy, market, bus stations, city bike, stations, parks, etc. 
We provide you a bicycle for the warm months (15 mins drive to Zavod Bob) and a monthly public transportation (bus) card for winter months. On average also 360€ monthly which covers food expenses and includes pocket money.

First two weeks of volunteering are “orientational weeks” in order to get to know a variety of activities at Zavod Bob. As a part of a volunteering project you will get a non-formal course of Slovenian language organized in a youth center. 
You will also have: 5 days on arrival training and 5 days mid-term evaluation training organized by the Slovenian national agency. You will also be involved in the final project evaluation session. During the volunteering there will be training opportunities (including international) according to personal interests, and organizational possibilities.

Searching for a person who is familiar with gardening and physical work in nature, who is close to ecological topics and able to bring them up in conversations and planning. They have to be keen on recycling and upcycling and find interests in creative and technical work, e.g. DIY workshops in green places and youth centers. We welcome a volunteer who is fluent in English, reliable, inclusive and likes to participate in group activities. Able to coexist in a flat with others. They also have to show initiative and find opportunities to contribute to the community. Driving license is a plus.

At Diggie, You take part in daily farm life: feeding the animals, cleaning the stables, gardening, and working together with other volunteers and visitors. As your Dutch improves, you can also help guide visiting groups and join children’s farm camps — assisting with cooking, games, and caring for the kids. Diggie is currently transitioning towards open youth work, meaning the farm will soon be open every weekend to young people and local visitors. You help shape this change and support the practical organization of these weekends. Depending on your interests, you can also develop creative projects such as filming short promo videos, or designing flyers. We value curiosity, teamwork, and the integration of each volunteer’s own creativity and ideas into the Diggie community!

The place of residence depends on the volunteer‘s preference. One option is to stay in Brakel, the small village. We will then look for a hosting family or a nearby place of residence. In this case we’ll also provide a bike to come to Diggie. Another option is that the volunteer lives in Gent, a city 30km away. Then we‘d search for a room or house to share with peers. From Gent the volunteer will have to take train and bus every day to come to Diggie. All costs of residence and transport will be payed by Diggie. The volunteer has to cook his/her own meal. We provide 180€ monthly for food.

We’ll teach you some specific skills needed on the farm. You will learn to heat up the wooden oven to bake bread and pizzas in it, how to make felt out of our sheep’s wool and butter/ice cream out of our neighbour farmer’s milk. The volunteers usually learn a lot from each other. We always have a nice mix of volunteers with less and more experience. We attach great importance to the volunteer learning Dutch as it greatly enhances the tasks you will have. You have in any case access to the Online Language Support, but we can also look for additional language courses.

We are looking for a creative and enthusiast all-round volunteer. Social skills and motivation are the most important characteristics. Education or experience in youth work, social work, farming or graphic design can be valuable, but aren’t necessary. We expect the volunteer to love animals and people, in particular children and people with special needs. He/she/they should like to work outside even when the weather is bad.
If you are interested send us a video where you tell us why you are the perfect fit for our beautiful farm an project. We love it creative 😊

YMCA Siderno is seeking enthusiastic volunteer English teachers to help empower our community. This opportunity is ideal for individuals who are motivated by the chance to build connections, share their language skills, and create meaningful change.

Solidarités Jeunesses (SJ) is a national movement of non-formal education and is composed of a National Secretary based in Paris, and eight regional delegations across France. Our delegations host volunteers from France and all over the world throughout the year. Each regional delegation is unique, but all of the activities organized benefit the local community and share common ground: 
- to gather people from different culture and social background to participate in social, ecological and cultural development on the local level . 
- To contribute to the integration of people with fewer opportunities. 
Each project is dedicated to actions of solidarity and collective living. We believe that cultural exchanges are a key for personal Learning and offers to the volunteer a valuable opportunity to learn, to experiment and to undergo personal development.

Sem&Vol is located in Cause de Clérans, in DORDOGNE, in the green center of France. Sem&Vol was founded in 2013 in the village of Le Buisson de Cadouin, for its first international project. The village is a small village of 300 inhabitants and is welcoming with volunteers. As a volunteer you will share a house with other volunteers! It is of high importance to commit into daily life, as in a big house-share, because the house will look like its inhabitants, it's your home sweet home for a few months!

You will work about 35 hours per week, the work is varied and you will get the support of the staff. We work on : Daily workcamp (minor masonry work, woodwork, painting, environmental work), Organisation and participation in local intercultural activities, local events, Building networks between local and our associations, Promotion of the association and volunteering, Leading international workcamps during the summer (training during the year is provided) Two seminars organized by the french agency and one volunteering meeting with all the volunteers of Solidarités Jeunesses.

There is no competencies required to participate but willingness to the volunteering project and being open to discover new cultures. Open to everybody from European Union or partner countries between 18/30 years old, the driving licence is HIGHLY recommended but what matters the most is the motivation ! So if you like MANUAL WORK, NATURE and COLLECTIVE LIFE, or if you're interested to discover it, contact us!

We are looking for 1 mushroom lover, who will work in this circular economy project called Café Vert! This project started years ago, with formation and lots of experimentation, and since 2020, our ESC volunteers are part of this experience. Our cooperative IDC's projects aim to raise awareness about the actual context we are living and to propose and create solutions to be part of a positive change in a social, cultural and environmental aspect. In this project especifically, we will reuse waste to create new life. We collect coffee waste from cafés and restaurants and mix it with mycellieum to grow oyster mushrooms. The volunteer for this mission will take care of the fruiting room and the mushrooms hospital at the eco-land, by monitoring their growth, harvest and sell them in a local market. And after harvesting, we use that new “waste” in our earth-worm farm, which is great to create new and rich soil for plants. Also, the volunteer will help in the animal care and other tasks!!

IDC is located in a small town, 20km from Carcassonne where the nearest train station and airport are (the volunteers will be picked from there and will be taken to the place). This region is rural, living mainly from wine farming and tourism. The place is surrounded by nature, so no shops. Accomodation: volunteers will stay in mobile homes, in shared-rooms, usually with another volunteer of the same sex. Food will be bought twice per month, and volunteers will cook healthy and low-impact food! following the food guidelines.

Volunteers will learn how to grow mushrooms from coffee waste (from the collection step to the selling of the products), how to maintain a fruiting room and harvest correctly, how to participate in local markets, and they will learn different sustainable practices to be more ethical and respectful with the environment. They will be able to lead them after or to propose new ideas/projects around sustainability, local and organic agriculture, intercultural exchange...

full_description:
As a volunteer, you will play a vital role in supporting caregivers and enriching the daily activities of our guests. Your contributions will help create a vibrant and engaging environment. 
Key Responsibilities:
Activity Preparation: Assist in gathering materials and ensuring that everything is ready for weekly activities.
Support Caregivers: Collaborate with caregivers in recreational and workshop activities, including cooking, digital storytelling, board games, library visits, music animation, and technology sessions.
Social Media Engagement: Create engaging posts and stories for our social networks to highlight events and activities.
Training Participation: Attend training sessions designed for experts and professionals in the field.
Community Engagement: Organize and participate in complementary activities with other volunteers
ESC Promotion: Promote the European Solidarity 
Support for Italian Volunteers: Assist in preparing Italian volunteers who are leaving for ESC

As a volunteer, you will live in a very modern and new furnitured flat together with 4 other volunteers from different countries, in the city of Pordenone just a walk away from the hosting organization. The accommodation will be provided in a single or double room with a shared bathroom and kitchen. You will receive 180 € pocket money and an extra 190€ as food money if you prepare all your meals. In this way you are free to cook in your fully equipped flat. You can get a bike under the deposit of 40€.

Volunteers will take part in the ESC training cycle organized by the Italian National Agency, in the Italian language course, in trainings offered in running educational and relational workshops.

Volunteer should be responsible, motivated, proactive, patient, tolerant and flexible to adapt to changes. Willing to work in an international social environment: firstly need to be high motivated to work with people with disability, secondly in the workshop activities and thirdly in living in Italy. Motivated to learn the Italian language. Determined to learn, dynamic, versatile, positive, curious, respectful, sensitive. Motivated for team work and educational paths. Able to share a flat with other young Europeans, or live with a host family and respect the rules. Passionate for the activities we offer. Volunteers should be aware that ESC is not a vacation, is not just travelling to another country but it is a full time learning experience in a safe environment.

By leaving your confort zone and joining our project, you can improve your french, your EU citizenship, discover a new culture and enjoy volunteering with a multicultural young team.

The main tasks of the volunteers will be :  
- to prepare and give presentations about their country, European mobility and the EU to different groups (pupils, students, adults, young people with fewer opportunities, etc.), to speak about their own experience and culture
- to welcome the general public at the office and during fairs and forums
- to promote the European Solidarity Corps and Erasmus+ to the youth of the region
- to create educational tools (e.g.games and posters) and new concepts for presentations 
- to help the team in the organisation of events (debates, Europe Day, European day of languages…) 
- to create cultural events with MUSIC, CIRCUS ARTS & GAMES, ACROBATICS, DANCES, 
- to raise awareness, especially among young people, about european and environmental issues

The volunteers will stay in a small student residence, where they will have their own room.  The Residence is located in the heart of the City Center of Amiens, at 3 minutes on foot far from the office. A Bike will be offered to each volunteer

The volunteers will get 14€/day for food and pocket money.

During their stay, the volunteers will take part in 2 seminars organised by the French National Agency. One on arrival and the other mid-stay. These seminars are mandatory for the volunteers who spend more than 6 months in our project. They will take place during a week, in south of France or in Paris

We are looking for highly-motivated volunteers from EU countries ready to commit ideally for a 4 months period but applications for shorter periods will also be considered. 

They will join a multicultural team of volunteers from all over the European Union.

Nous sommes à la recherche de volontaires désireux de vivre dans une communauté multiculturelle, adeptes de la vie en communauté, motivés pour soutenir l'environnement/localité locale et l'organisation. Les volontaire participeront :

-À la récolte d'invendus au marché de Thessalonique
-Aux potentiels projets mis en place par l'association au moment de la mission.

L'hébergement se fera dans des chambres partagées. Aucune allocation alimentaire ne sera donnée aux volontaires, car les volontaires mangent ensemble.
Des vélos seront fournis aux volontaires par l'organisation moyennant une petite caution ou en échange de réparations.

Le volontaire a 2 jours de congés par semaine, ils sont variables en fonction des activités de l’association.

We are offering a 4- or 8 month volunteer project starting on 01-05-26. Initially, participants commit to a 4-month contract, during which we will evaluate the experience together with the volunteer, the professionals they collaborate with, and our organization. 

This project allows participants to explore various aspects of social work, with a focus on supporting individuals with different types of limitations. We are looking for volunteers who are enthusiastic about working in the social sector. Applicants with an educational background in social work are especially encouraged to apply.
An interest in gardening and sports activities is highly valued. Since effective communication is crucial in the social field, a willingness to learn Dutch is a significant advantage.
For detailed information about the project, please refer to our info kit available on our website: www.lava-group.com. Simply scroll down to the "International Volunteer Work" section to find the info kit link.

Volunteers stay in two cozy locations: a big shared house in Zoetermeer that can host up to eight people, and a smaller apartment in Rotterdam for four. The hosting organisation takes care of the placements, so volunteers don’t need to worry about choosing where they’ll stay.
Everyone has their own private bedroom, while the kitchen and bathroom are shared with housemates. A bicycle is provided for getting around day to day, and volunteers receive €400 per month to cover food and pocket money.

During the project, volunteers have many opportunities to learn and grow. A Dutch language course is offered throughout the project period, and motivated, engaged volunteers are especially encouraged to take part. Before departure, volunteers are prepared for the different groups of people they will work with by discussing real-life cases and learning how to approach various situations.
In addition, the Dutch NA  provides all participating volunteers with on-arrival and mid-term training sessions, offering further opportunities to connect, share experiences, and develop new skills.

IMPORTANT NOTE! For this project we can only host EU citizens!!!  We look for volunteers who have a proven interest in the social sector, who are interested in working with people with limitations. An educational background in the social field, could be an advantage but is not a requirement. The willingness to learn the Dutch language, before arrival is a big bonus, since communication is important in the social sector. All communication will take place in English, so it is important to understand English and/or have a strong motivation to learn English in a rapid speed, prior to arrival. The volunteer will work for different organisations/locations: flexibility to work for different organisations is therefore a necessity.

Our Krishnamurti-inspired education centre for children in the North of Portugal, O Mundo Somos Nós (www.instagram.com/omundosomosnos), is looking for long-term volunteers (6 months) starting in January 2026.
Beyond the daily physical tasks of supporting our staff around meal times and helping with small repairs and maintenance tasks around the centre, we organise weekly Dialogue sessions. During these sessions we have the space to go into topics like responsibility, relationships, awareness, and more. Each week we set a focus topic to sit with and inquire throughout the week. Additionally, we provide a variety of physical and digital resources for extra guidance and going deeper.
Through practical involvement in our daily operations, volunteers participate in the greater service of providing a loving space for our young ones to grow and flourish. Each moment becomes an invitation to become fully present.
No previous experience required, just a genuine interest in changing oneself.

Our volunteers are accommodated at the local pilgrims hostel “Albergue de Peregrinos S. Pedro”. The Albergue is within a walking distance from OMSN. The volunteers will have their own reserved area within the Albergue with Wi-Fi connection. OMSN provides vegetarian lunches during weekdays and the hostel kitchen can be used to prepare any additional meals. In accordance with the ESC program, a monthly allowance for food and pocket money of €270 will be provided on a monthly basis. The travel expenses will be reimbursed based on the distance bands defined by the ESC Programme Guide.

During their stay, our volunteers receive training and mentoring provided by OMSN to enhance their integration into the project. The weekly Dialogue sessions are a central activity of the project. The volunteers have the space for dialogue and inquiry into their own experience and inner world. The focus is always on direct observation without ideologies. Additionally, a Portuguese language course is offered via the OLS platform before their arrival and throughout their stay in Portugal. The volunteers will be able to practice their Portuguese at OMSN while engaging in activities with children.

We are looking for volunteers who are: 1.​ between 18 and 30 years old; 2.​ eager to learn and motivated to work on the proposed activities of OMSN; 3.​ demonstrating kindness, humility, responsibility, motivation, and focus; 4.​ willing to learn Portuguese; 5.​ willing to live in a rural place 30-40 minutes from the next bigger city. Because OMSN's activities involve working with young children, we will consider the age, maturity, and willingness of the volunteer to commit to a long-term experience abroad.

More than anything, we are looking for young people who are truly interested in looking at themselves clearly and inquire into the dynamics of the Self and the Ego. We are not a place of religion, methods, or ideologies. But we are serious about Self-Knowledge and the direct observation of reality because we realise that changing ourselves is the only way to create lasting positive change in the world. And to change ourselves, first we have to learn about ourselves. Not by following what someone else told us, but by looking at ourselves and finding out directly.

If this sounds like you, I am more than happy to receive your application!

- Mi-term training organized by Italian National Agency

Young people between 18 and 29 years old who are EU citizens or legally residing in EU.

Please note: In accordance with the Programme, this project shall include young people not in employment, education or training (N.E.E.T.) and/or with fewer opportunities.

AVEC is an association focused on children, adolescents and young adults. Their office and youth center is based in Maamoura, a small beach town close to the city of Nabeul. They organise workshops for children in different domains. They’re also very active in international exchanges and capacity building projects, training local volunteers to become powerful international changemakers.

Proactive

The aim of this ESC project (11 months) is to introduce young people to the reality of out-of-school education institution and its activities, help them improve their skills and abilities, foreign language while at the same time allowing them to learn new ones. For some this can also be the first time they are out of their home, in a foreign country and on their own. We are here to help them with all of those things. Volunteers will help them with ongoing activities prepared by the Centre for leisure time activities. The volunteers are able to use their kitchen to cook food or they can join us for regular lunch at one of the restaurants (or some common lunches / celebrations). They are also provided with monthly sum of money in addition to the pocket money.

On arrival training roughly weeks to about 2 months after their arrival, to be conducted by our National Agency (place and time chosen by the NA, changes all the time) with other volunteers staying in the country. Followed by Mid-term training somewhere in the middle of their stay (roughly 4-5 months after On arrival training). Daily lessons in Slovak language with a designated teacher/tutor as needed.

We are looking for volunteers that are still children in their hearts, open to new situations and things and who also want to work with children and the youth in the area of culture and eductation. Young people that will tolerante different cultures and those that are prepared by their sending organisation – to stay longer time without their family in another country. At least basic level of English is very welcome and helpful. As is having experience working with children and the youth and/or ability to dance, have interesting ideas, organize activities and a lot of patience. If you enjoy managing social media and doing photos/videos that is also a plus. You will have an easier time if you can fill some of the emptier moments with your own activities or work.

Volunteering within our project involves engaging in daily non-formal educational, child-centered activities for children and young people from day centers, schools for kids with special needs, nurseries, primary schools, after-school programs, and kindergartens in disadvantaged areas of Reșița (Calnic), Bocșa, Dognecea, and Ocna de Fier. Volunteers will help facilitate learning experiences that foster tolerance, inclusion, and social skills. Additionally, we organize cultural and volunteering activities that promote values such as solidarity and voluntary work, and encourage positive interaction within the community. During the summer, volunteers will take part as team members in short-term projects, wearing personalized t-shirts, where they will have the opportunity to lead teams and help facilitate team-building activities, allowing them to improve their leadership and collaboration skills.

The accommodation will be fully equipped with all necessary amenities to ensure comfortable living conditions, including access to a kitchen, bathroom, and communal living space. All housing costs, including rent and utilities (water, gas, electricity), will be fully covered by the hosting NGO. Additionally, the NGO will provide support for local transportation, as well as daily allowances for food and personal expenses. 4 EUR/day as pocket money 5 EUR/day as a food allowance.

The training will be provided by the Romanian National Agency. Volunteers will participate in an On-Arrival Training held online, and a Mid-Term Training conducted in person in Bucharest.
