full_description:
Wir bieten engagierten Naturschützern zwischen 18 und 30 Jahre die Möglichkeit eines Volontariats auf Sizilien, Bronte zur Unterstützung der kleinen Naturschutzorganisation „Giacche Verdi Bronte“ bei vielfältigen Tätigkeiten. 
In den kleinbäuerlich geprägten Flusstälern zwischen Ätna und Nebrodi-Gebirge arbeiten wir an der Errichtung eines Biosphärenreservats und führen verschiedene Umweltbildungsprojekte mit Kindern sowie praktische, planerische und experimentelle Naturschutzaktivitäten und landwirtschaftliche Arbeiten durch. Es finden außerdem Erhebungen zur Artenvielfalt statt. Generell helfen alle Volontäre in allen Projekten. Schwerpunkt bei Giacche Verdi ist die Umweltbildung für Kinder. Weitere Aktivitäten sind praktische Arbeiten im Feld (Olivenernte, Bäume pflanzen, Mähen usw.) oder liegen in Bereichen der Dokumentation und Öffentlichkeitsarbeit, Recherchen oder Monitoring. 
Zeitraum der möglichen Entsendung besprechen wir individuell.

Die Aufnahmeorganisation kann derzeit bis zu 6 europäische Freiwillige aufnehmen und beherbergt weitere Freiwillige aus anderen Programmen. Die Unterkunft ist schlicht aber praktikabel, es gibt Mehrbettzimmer, eine Gemeinschaftsküche und -Bad. Die Volontäre erhalten i.d.R. Verpflegunsgeld und versorgen sich selbst. Die Mobilität vor Ort geschieht zu Fuß, per Bus und Bahn und über die Aufnahmeorganisation. Die klimafreundliche An-un Abreise per Zug wird i.d.R. pauschal erstattet.

Was bringt Dir der Freiwilligendienst? Du gewinnst vielfältige neue Eindrücke in einer anderen Kultur, erweiterst Sprachkenntnisse, soziale Kompetenzen und Wissen, machst neue Erfahrungen und Freundschaften, erprobst deine Fähigkeiten und lernst neue dazu.Das Volontariat ist weder Urlaubsreise noch Fortbildung, sondern ein aktiver Einsatz, der deinen Horizont erweitern wird und Dich persönlich wachsen lässt, wenn Du Dich auf das „Abenteuer Sizilien“ voll und ganz einlässt.

Du bist an Naturschutz interessiert, freundlich, offen, teamfähig, engagiert, selbstständig und flexibel. Wichtig sind außerdem Anpassungs- und Lernfähigkeit, Fairness, Respekt der anderen Mentalität des Gastlandes gegenüber und Bescheidenheit. Italienischkenntnisse sind ein Vorteil aber kein Muss.

Adichats works to preserve and promote our natural and built heritage. We even run several medieval castles. The Castles, and mostly the Villandraut’s Castel represent for us the perfect spot to organize events and create social bonds.

Your missions:

First, you'll dive into a feasibility study exploring how to create microclimates which can remain viable even with a temperature rise of 2 to 4 degrees. You'll also look into using natural materials and decarbonized building techniques to restore local heritage sites and probably anticipate the future of buildings.

Next, you'll help develop an economic strategy model that can be applied to various territories, ultimately aiding in the creation of these microclimates.

Ultimately, we will need you on a day-to-day basis for the association's and the castle's activities during the summer (visits, events, annual festival gathering between 2000 and 3000 visitors as well as restoration and cleaning of the castle).

You will be welcomed to the charming village of Villandraut, South Gironde. 1,000 awesome residents call it home. Villandraut has all the essential local shops and services. You're not in this adventure alone! You'll be with other super cool European volunteers. But here's the twist – get ready for some countryside living: public transport is as rare as a shooting star around, but fear not! We've got a car and bicycles to share. We also work with a local organisation that set up a carpooling platform + meal allowance to keep your energy levels maxed out!

1. Super training : technical & educational training sessions offered by Union REMPART and our awesome partner networks. 
2. Personalized Boost : We're here for you! You'll get personalized support, including orientation sessions, one-on-one chats, and all sorts of tips and tricks to help you level up. We'll make your missions feel like a breeze. We can adjust them based on your goals & dreams. 
4. Epic team : You won't be alone in this adventure. You'll team up with other ESC volunteer and  French volunteers on a mission. Together, you'll create some awesome projects.

We're on the hunt for a passionate volunteer with a background or a true interest in Earth Sciences or Geography!
If you've got some skills in planning workshops or a deep passion for heritage and environmental issues, consider that a bonus point! But here's the deal: what really matters is your enthusiasm, openness, and a good attitude. If you're a high-energy individual, this is the place to be! We're not just a group; we're a team. So, what are you waiting for? Jump on board! We're all about embracing diverse interests – whether you're an artist, a nature enthusiast, or anyone else ! Get ready for a LIFE-CHANGING ADVENTURE! We just need to make sure you're all set for rural living.

Dinamización de la Vega Granadina is an individual volunteering project which aims to dynamize the rural world in the area of la Vega de Granada through activities of non-formal education, environmental action and intercultural living.

Accomodation, food and transport are included.

Training during the opportunity is included in different areas.

We are looking for a motivated person who likes to work in teams. A proactive participant willing to support all the activities proposed by the organisation in the rural areas of Granada.
It is important for the candidate to speak English and to have some basic knowledge of Spanish.

Alianza por la Solidaridad, member of ActionAid, aims to achieve an active citizenship that fights against inequalities and for the recognition of human rights. Alianza's work in Palestine focuses on promoting human rights and combating gender-based violence from a holistic perspective, including awareness-raising, improving opportunities for women and multi-sectoral care for survivors of gender-based violence, among others. Join us at our offices in Palestine! You will have the chance to contribute to improving the processes and procedures related to the administration and finances of the organization together with a professional and experienced team. At the end of your experience, you will be familiar with the preparation of budgets and the financial monitoring and justification of projects as a whole. You will work with local partners in Gaza Strip, West Bank and East Jerusalem. Alianza's partners are among the strongest ones in the context and work with high quality commitment

You will have the opportunity to live with other people but with individual bedroom. The accommodation costs and utility bills will be covered by the organization. A phone card be provided. The house will be in Amman. You will receive a monthly allowance of 813,70€ for your personal expenses, including food and local transport. There is freedom of movement but always complying with the security directives. You will also be covered with a health insurance (Henner)

You will receive training which will cover topics such as: induction to Alianza por la Solidaridad, induction to the European Solidarity Corps, responsibilities and rights of the organisations and of the volunteer, Youthpass, Henner insurance and SHEA. In addition you will be trained more specifically in feminist principles and other training opportunities which may include: International Humanitarian Law, security management, gender, disabilities, etc.).

We are looking for a person eager to learn and work in a team and able to adapt to a multicultural and diverse environment respecting the different cultures in Palestine and Jordan. Interest in developing skills in administration and finance, familiar with the principles and tools of this discipline. Knowledge in development cooperation, humanitarian aid or any previous experience will be an asset. Fluent in English, able to adapt to complex situations. If you are migrant, live in rural areas, have limited economic support… don´t hesitate to sign up, this opportunity is for everyone!

As a child and youth welfare organisation, VSD as the parent company of Charly's Kinderparadies sees it as its responsibility to promote voluntary work in relevant solidary social projects by providing adequate placements in the European Soldarity Corps such as the kindergartens of Charly's Kinderparadies. As part of an ongoing process of internationalisation, both in the economy and society in general and directly within the company, the aim is also to make a contribution to an open, democratic and tolerant Europe. In addition, the temporary integration of the participants into the everyday life of the children in the kindergarden can provide important impetus and contribute to a positive development in living together. The contact between the children and the volunteers from other ethnic groups and cultures can strengthen "togetherness" and team spirit.

Volunteers will receive comprehensive support throughout their experience, from arrival to departure, ensuring they feel comfortable and well-guided. Meals are provided, with the meal allowance paid in cash or via EC card. Additionally, to facilitate mobility, the cost of the transport ticket for local public transportation will be reimbursed upon submission of proof.  The cost of the flight ticket for arrival and departure will be fully covered by us.

To further enhance the experience, we also offer opportunities for personal and professional development, including workshops, skill-building sessions, and guidance on navigating the local culture and administrative systems. Volunteers can participate in networking events to connect with local organizations and other volunteers, fostering collaboration and exchange. Additionally, we provide ongoing feedback and support to ensure that volunteers not only succeed in their roles but also gain valuable insights and skills for their future endeavors.

Volunteers are engaged in the field of early childhood education, where they have the opportunity to share aspects of their own culture with the children, fostering openness and curiosity towards people from different backgrounds from an early age. The volunteers support the professionals in their daily work in their own mother tongue. The pedagogical concept of Charly's Kinderparadies provides the framework for this. They make contact with the children during their daily play and accompany them in the centre, help them get dressed and offer various play opportunities. In the care area, the volunteers help to serve meals, feed individual children and offer them assistance. In addition, they contribute ideas for new projects, taking into account the children's interests, and support the professionals in the planning and implementation of these projects, which can also take place over a longer period of time. Games, songs and other activities can be planned and carried out. We prefer candidates who have graduated from a vocational school or university in early childhood education.

***Please note that this vacancy is only open to volunteers who currently reside in the Netherlands; you do not need to be Dutch, but you must be able to provide proof of registration in the Netherlands.***

Imagine spending a few months in sunny southern Spain, near the sea, in a charming rural town, learning Spanish and making a real difference in the community. We’re looking for two motivated volunteers from the Netherlands to join our solidarity project in Albuñol, Andalusia. You’ll engage with children through games, sports, and creative workshops, support elderly residents with daily tasks or companionship, and assist people with disabilities in their daily activities. Most work is Monday to Friday, with occasional weekend events. Spanish (A2-B1) is recommended to fully enjoy life here. If you’re flexible, eager, and ready for a meaningful adventure, this is your chance to grow, connect, and contribute!

Accommodation and conditions
Shared house in Albuñol:
Furnished private bedroom
Shared kitchen, bathroom, and living room
Internet and bed linen included
Food and pocket money: you’ll receive a monthly allowance to buy your own food and other essentials, so you can cook according to your taste and needs.
Local transport: all activities are within walking distance (max. 25 minutes). For work activities outside the village, transportation will be provided. You can also use local buses or BlaBlaCar for personal trips.

Training is provided by the Spanish national agency. Different organisations that you work for, will provide support and training on the job. 
Pre-departure meetings and interview are organised prepare you before arrival. 
Mentor support is provided throughout the project. Together with your mentor you can discuss what possible learning opportunities are available and/or can be created for instance through the adult education centre.

We are looking for enthusiastic and flexible volunteers who are eager to help, enjoy staying active, and are motivated to practice and improve their Spanish. Many local children love football, so an interest in sports, especially football, is a big plus!
Albuñol is a small, welcoming community where very few people speak English. Volunteers should be independent, adaptable, and open to immersing themselves in Spanish language and culture. While living here requires flexibility and independence, Granada is just a 2-hour bus ride away, and the beautiful beach is only 8km away.
This project offers a unique chance to grow personally, connect deeply with the community, and make a real difference. If you’re ready to embrace the challenges, you’ll find it an incredibly rewarding experience.

Over 35years that GDCA has mapped out long-term prospects to raise funds and resources to ensure its continuous existence in bringing education and opportunities to the vulnerable and marginalised in society. 
Digital literacy is key for accessing information, communication, and jobs. The Digital Literacy Advisor will equip youth and women with essential digital skills, fostering innovation, employability, and entrepreneurship while bridging the digital divide. GDCA supports youth and women empowerment through vocational training. The advisor will integrate digital skills into these programs to prepare participants for the workforce and evolving technologies.

Tasks:
Deliver digital literacy training
Guide participants in using digital tools
Identify digital needs and design tailored training
Integrate digital skills into vocational programs
Monitor and evaluate impact
Develop digital learning resources
Promote digital literacy for empowerment

GDCA will organize accommodation close the office as possible, comprising a self-contained apartment with soft furnishing and with individual bath and toilet facilities. Basic kitchen facilities will be provided. GDCA will provide transport for official duties. The personal movement and food of the volunteer will be borne by the volunteer under the framework of the agreement of the volunteer programme.

The BRIDGE project (Building Resilience, Innovation, Development, and Gender Equality) enables volunteers to empower vulnerable communities, focusing on women and digital skills. They will attend UN Women Summits, lead digital workshops, and support skills development. Key topics include digital literacy, gender diversity, leadership in tech, digital safety, and financial literacy for digital entrepreneurship. The project promotes social cohesion, inclusion, and digital empowerment in a rapidly evolving world.

Candidates must be 18 to 35 years old, reside in one of the eligible countries (EU Member State, North Macedonia, Iceland, Liechtenstein or Turkey), have completed the compulsory Humanitarian Aid Volunteering training and not have participated before in individual Humanitarian Aid Volunteering. When adding together this new volunteering opportunity and any previous participation in EU volunteering programmes, the total duration cannot exceed 12 months.
Qualifications and Skills:
1.	Appreciated Educational Qualifications: Degree in information technology, Computer Science, Education, Social Sciences, or a related field 
2.	Desired Experience: 
- Experience in digital skills training, technology education, or community development is highly desirable
- Experience working with youth, women, or marginalized groups is an advantage.
- Previous experience in NGOs, social enterprises, or governmental projects related to digital inclusion is a plus.

3.	Skills and Competencies:
Technical Skills: Proficiency in using digital tools, software, and online platforms.
Communication Skills: Ability to explain technical concepts in simple terms and engage diverse audiences.
Organizational Skills: Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize activities, and meet deadlines.
Interpersonal Skills: Empathy, active listening, and the ability to build rapport with participants.
Problem-Solving and Critical Thinking: Ability to address challenges and adapt training methods to meet participants’ needs.
Cultural Sensitivity: Awareness and respect for cultural differences, especially when working with underserved populations.
Data Management Skills: Experience in collecting and analyzing data for program monitoring and evaluation.
Knowledge of Digital Inclusion Frameworks: Familiarity with local and international initiatives promoting digital literacy and inclusion.

The Santiago Uno Home-School is an organization dedicated to working with minors at risk of social exclusion. Through our own therapeutic model, we address the diverse needs and problems that today's youth experience in their lives in society.
Our work focuses on the different social environments of children in order to provide close and ongoing interventions, offering each individual the opportunity to discover themselves and acquire new skills that will allow them to fully develop. To this end, we carry out various projects based on educational training, healthy leisure activities, sports, a circus school, a theater school, cultural exchanges, and many other projects with which we aim to offer our youth an alternative way of life.

Volunteer accommodation is provided in a rented apartment or in an apartment owned by the organization itself, with all utilities included (internet, electricity, heating, furniture, etc.).
The main meal is served in the organization's dining room, together with the youth and educators. A monthly stipend is provided for breakfast and dinner.
For transportation, volunteers are given a city bus pass and, if preferred, a bicycle for getting around the city.

The volunteers' tasks are very varied and evolve as the project progresses. Initially, they are accompanied as they participate in the Casa Escuela activities, demonstrating how it works and supporting them during their adaptation period. They are asked to answer questions, introduce them to other professionals from the organization, and facilitate connections with the participating youth. Be part of a meaningful experience where you can learn, share, and grow alongside a passionate team. Alianza por la Solidaridad, ActionAid member, aims to achieve an active citizenship that fights against inequalities and for the recognition of human rights. It carries out development cooperation and education projects to eradicate gender-based violence, enhance migrants' rights and for climate justice. Join us at our office in Mauritania! You will have the opportunity to support a dedicated team of professionals. Your tasks will include assisting in project formulation, report preparation, and managing relevant information to support ongoing activities. You will also take part in fieldwork to collect data and help implement project actions.Additionally, you will contribute to initiatives promoting women’s rights supporting the organization and planning of strategies for rural women, providing gender-sensitive inputs, and helping to develop or review training and awareness-raising materials.

The volunteer will share accommodation with other volunteers in a multicultural environment with access to her/ his own individual bedroom. The accommodation costs and utility bills will be covered by the organization. To cover all day-to-day costs such as food the volunteer will be provided with a monthly allowance of 569,27€. For your participation in the activities of Alianza, a vehicle will be provided. Furthermore, you will have a health insurance that will cover all your health expenses during your stay. We have built the most favourable environment to provide you with a unique stay.

As a volunteer in Alianza you will receive training which will cover topics such as: induction to our ONG as well as an induction to the European Solidarity Corps programme. In addition, you will be trained more specifically in feminist leadership and our own working policies. In the end of your volunteering, you will know how to work in a multidisciplinary team, both on the field and in the office, as well as you will have had acquired specific training related to the projects we implement strengthening your professional profile in areas such as agro-ecology, social action or women's rights.

We are looking for a person eager to learn and work in a team and able to adapt to new contexts. We are looking for a person with knowledge in gender. We are looking for a motivated person who looking forward to work in the field with the beneficiary population and to contribute his/her knowledge in the implementation of projects. Experience in the project cycle would also be an advantage. French is a must and Spanish is an asset. If you are migrant, live in rural areas, have limited economic support or any other don´t hesitate to sign up, this opportunity is for everyone!

Young European volunteers from different countries will participate in activities developed in important natural areas, living together with the local community and working side by side in a local volunteer team. Intercultural issues, the value of cultural diversity, the exchange of experiences, the mutual enrichment, the respect and tolerance will be promoted. Fieldwork: The volunteers will actively collaborate in our scientific bird monitoring programs (census and marking) in Doñana and several projects of habitat restoration and conservation campaigns in Doñana and other natural areas. From the Francisco Bernis Bird Centre, we develop awareness campaigns and environmental education programs among the local community. The volunteers also will collaborate with visitor management staff in the Francisco Bernis Bird Centre.

Food: The volunteer will receive every month 160 € for food. Accommodation: Private room in a shared accommodation with other young people. The accommodation will be fully equipped and electricity, water, gas will be covered by the hosting organization. The practical arrangements (working hours, days off per week, holidays): The volunteer works 35 hours on 5 days per week. There is an entitlement to holidays for 2 days per month, altogether holidays days that can be taken after consulting with the SEO/BirdLife team.

The volunteers will receive training seminars including detailed information on all the activities in which they will collaborate, as well as the natural and social environment in which it develops. We also organize workshops and information sessions. The volunteers will receive short courses on ecology, biology, species identification, and marking and monitoring of species. Language support: The volunteer is entitled to receive a language support with an online platform, as stated on the Erasmus+ programme guide

Participants should be young and highly motivated volunteers, showing special interest in the conservation and study of the environment. Willingness to cooperate, personal initiative, a positive attitude to collaborate in fieldwork, tolerance, respect for the customs and culture of the other volunteers and the local community, as well as the sense of humor will be highly appreciated. Applicants must have a good general health. Once the recruitment process is opened, volunteers fulfilling the above mentioned profile will be shortlisted.

This opportunity consists in restoring the nesting sites of the roller by protecting and planting cavity trees, by installing and maintaining artificial nesting boxes, and by sensitizing the local actors to reduce the agricultural intensification and the use of pesticides. 
On the other hand, it consists in participating in the monitoring of the population of rollers in the Vallée des Baux. This consists of locating and monitoring the reproduction of breeding pairs, participating in the ringing of birds, participating in scientific research programs on the species, and managing the database for monitoring the roller.
Other tasks will include French language courses, time spent communicating about the European Solidarity Corps through various actions (video, stands, articles), tasks related to the daily life of the A Rocha France Center.

The volunteers are housed at the study centre, which is also the logistic base for the projects, the head office and the hub for running the life of the team. They share rooms (1 to 2 people of the same sex per room). Lunch and supper are eaten together during the week with the team and any other participants at fixed times. Breakfasts are self-service. The team members take turns at preparing the meals for the group. Special diets are catered for. The centre is no-smoking. Bikes are available for getting around. Rules of life might be adapted due to the COVID situation.

Training will be provided at arrival concerning the rules of life at the center, community life, week planning and project and activity description. Field work training is provided all along the project to the volunteer such as: species identification skills, protocols, use of observation tools and other field equipment. Training in database management, data analysis and report drafting is also provided depending on the volunteer skills at arrival.

We are looking for volunteers who have a real interest in protecting the environment. They will need to enjoy life in the country and the contact with the flora and fauna, which means sometimes putting up with difficult conditions, getting around by bike, the wind, dry heat, etc. The volunteers will have to show that they can take initiatives in the tasks they undertake and take them through to completion. They should not hesitate to ask for clarification or direction if necessary for their projects. A basic knowledge of French and a full driving licence are an advantage for the volunteers.

As part of the European Solidarity Corps, our project offers young people from across Europe a chance to engage in meaningful long-term volunteering. You’ll work closely with a supportive team of educators, helping to create a rich learning environment for children aged 3–6 — mostly outdoors, in all seasons. You’ll assist in daily activities, prepare creative workshops, care for our garden and outdoor space, and even design your own mini-project to benefit the school or the local community.

Volunteers are accommodated in a shared flat in a nearby town, with access to all basic amenities. They receive a monthly food allowance and pocket money according to ESC standards. Local transport costs related to project activities are covered, and bicycles are available. Upon arrival, volunteers are guided through the area to help them orient themselves and settle in comfortably.

You’ll be encouraged to reflect on your learning journey through regular mentoring, teamwork, and structured sessions using Youthpass. You’ll also have time for personal growth, intercultural exchange, language learning You’ll also have time for personal growth, intercultural exchange, language learning, and building real friendships.
We especially welcome volunteers with fewer opportunities or those seeking a transformative experience in a supportive, inclusive, and nature-connected setting. At Studánka, we believe that "Studánka isn’t just a kindergarten… it’s a real world."

We welcome open-minded, curious, and responsible young people aged 18–30 who are motivated to work with children in a nature-based environment. No specific experience is required — just a willingness to learn, collaborate in a team, and step outside your comfort zone. Creativity, empathy, and a sense of initiative are highly valued. This project is especially suitable for those interested in alternative education, outdoor learning, and community life.

Union Plaani will host four ESC volunteers in Heinola, Finland from 7 January to 31 May 2026. The project promotes solidarity, inclusion and community engagement through grassroots football, youth activities and intercultural exchange. Volunteers will support Union Plaani’s programs for children and young people, contribute to community events such as Plaanilandia, and collaborate with local schools and partners.

The project provides volunteers with opportunities for personal growth, teamwork and intercultural learning, while bringing new perspectives and cultural diversity to the local community. The JFE Anna Landsberger is located in Marzahn-Hellersdorf, Berlin. Our center welcomes young people to spend their free time and take part in non-formal activities such as graffiti, painting, cooking, making music, playing ping-pong, doing sports, handicrafts, and political education.

Our project invites volunteers to socialise with young visitors, spend time with them, support their talents, and help them with their needs whenever possible. In addition, we offer volunteers educational opportunities such as international exchanges.
JFE Anna Landsberger is open Monday to Friday from 13:00 to 21:00. Volunteers will support the team and young people for 6 hours a day. 
https://roter-baum.berlin/international/open-calls/

We provide an apartment very close to the project. You will have your own bedroom and shared common spaces with other volunteers. Kampala School for the Physically Handicapped (KSPH) is a primary school catering to the educational needs of disabled children in Uganda. Started in 1968 by a few parents of cerebral palsied children, the school aims at educating, rehabilitating and equipping physically handicapped children for self-reliance and development. It follows the national syllabus including co-curricular activities like sports, music, dance and drama, spiritual fellowship, and educational tours.
It also offers vocational subjects like tailoring, screen printing, craft, tie-dye, and computer training to all children who cannot continue with further education. The school has an enrollment of 100 pupils with physical disabilities between the ages of 6–18, including those with cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, spina bifida, and polio among others.
Therefore, the school specifically provides for children with special needs. It has a teaching staff of 13 teachers.

Volunteers will stay at Villa Mamu, Mengo, Kampala, a  residence with WiFi, a warm shower, a kitchen, and pets. The volunteer shall prepare their own meals and living in own room. Other accommodation options in Kampala can be arranged based on safety and convenience. Local transport mainly consists of boda-bodas (motorcycle taxis). The project is in Kampala and in a walkable distance from Villa Mamu

Training includes skills development workshops, digital literacy enhancement, participation in UN Women Summits, and facilitating digital training sessions. Volunteers will gain hands-on experience in capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and social impact-driven project execution while refining leadership and communication skills.

Skills Advantage: Having experience in caring for children with special needs, or occupational and physiotherapy skills, is an added advantage.

¿Te gustaría descubrir cómo se crean y gestionan los proyectos europeos que conectan a jóvenes de toda Europa? 
Con DYPALL Network, podrás formar parte de un equipo internacional dinámico, donde tus ideas cuentan y cada día trae algo nuevo.

Como persona voluntaria en gestión de proyectos, apoyarás al equipo en la organización y desarrollo de actividades, la coordinación de eventos y formaciones, y la redacción de proyectos Erasmus+ y del Cuerpo Europeo de Solidaridad. Durante esta aventura, aprenderás cómo funciona el “backstage” de los proyectos internacionales, desarrollarás tus habilidades de comunicación, planificación y trabajo en equipo, y vivirás una experiencia intercultural única en el sur de Portugal. Valoramos especialmente a quienes disfrutan trabajando en grupo, organizando actividades y aportando ideas nuevas. También se apreciarán las habilidades de comunicación, redacción, organización y uso básico de herramientas digitales.

The place is off-grid, fulfilling basic needs, and participants must approach this with a non-wasteful mindset. Common areas include the living room, kitchen, shower and toilets. No specific experience is needed—just a love of living in an offgrid, forest environment, a willingness to work physically, and an open mindset. You’ll gain practical experience and learn about preparing old buildings for renovation, and contribute to a meaningful project.

Let’s create a future rooted in nature—growing it together, one project at a time

Serra Guarneri is an environmental education center located in the Madonie Mountains. Part of Palma Nana social cooperative, we work with kids and adults to teach environmental awareness, conservation, sustainable tourism, permaculture, circular economy, community living, and much more. A tiny village in the woods, we live as a community and embody our teaching, living simply and in tune with our surroundings and neighbors. Volunteers are expected to become apart of this community, taking part in diverse activities and caring for the structure, village, inhabitants, and local community. The project is rooted in revitalizing rural life by encouraging creativity and equipping participants with practical skills for sustainable living. 
During much of the year, the structure hosts groups of children and adults, who come for school camps, summer camps, environmental trainings, yoga retreats, and more. Our priority of the project is caring for these guests and teaching them our way of life.

In a rural contexr, volunteers live in a 3-bedroom structure with other volunteers, max 2/room. There is a shared bathroom and kitchen, shared with other guests and community members as needed. There's no AC, and heating is from a wood stove in winter Meals are usually prepared by staff and shared with guests. Staff purchase breakfast items and any additional food necessary for volunteers weekly. Food is mainly vegetarian, local, in season, and organic. Volunteers should arrive with green travel. There is a bus stop 45 mins by foot in the nearby village, which can take you to the train station

Training takes place in the context of the practical work, and you will learn based on your interests and what you involve yourself in. 

Things you could learn at Serra Guarneri: environmental education philosophy and activities; Sicilian recipes and low-waste cooking; foraging and local plants; cleaning and upkeep of rural structures; hospitality and sustainable tourism; Sicilian culture and traditions; low-budget construction, maintenance, and renovation; organic/permaculture gardening; circular economy & closed-loop systems; alternative economy.

Volunteers must have personal motivation to engage in community living, must take initiative and responsibility, and are enthusiastic about becoming an essential part of an ecological community that hosts guests on a daily basis. The project is for those who are able to live with less comforts in a rural setting, can adapt to a different culture, are good at problem solving. Volunteers must be flexible to daily work, as plans can change often. Experience in practical work, cleaning, and gardening is a plus. Diese Einrichtungen sind für die außerschulische Erziehung der Kinder zuständig. Insgesamt sind etwa 5.000 Kinder in den verschiedenen Häusern eingeschrieben. Die Aufgaben der EV: 
- Artikel und Fotos der Kinder zu sammeln und zusammenstellen
- in ständigem Kontakt mit den Fachkräften in den Einrichtungen zu stehen !
- die Kinder bei der Erstellung der Artikel zu unterstützen 
- die Veröffentlichung der Zeitung mit der Druckerei zu koordinieren 
- das Design der Zeitung in ADOBE InDesign zu entwickeln; dabei werden Sie von einem Grafiker unterstützt 
Kontakt: Mail: sven.gorza@croix-rouge.lu Tel.: +352621395992

Die EV wird in einem Haus mit sieben anderen Freiwilligen untergebracht. Jeder Freiwillige hat sein eigenes Zimmer. Das Wohnzimmer, die Küche, die Waschküche, die Dusche und die Toilette werden gemeinsam genutzt. Jede Etage verfügt über ein eigenes Bad. Das Haus befindet sich in Betzdorf, mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln ist das Büro in 60 Minuten zu erreichen. Die Kosten für das Essen und den Transport sind im Taschengeld enthalten. - mit externen und internen Projektpartnern zusammenzuarbeiten

- gute deutsche Sprachkenntnisse (min B1)
- ein polizeiliches Führungszeugnis zu haben

This 2 or 6-12 month project is designed for youth who want to experience life in an Ecovillage and farm in rural Sweden. The volunteers' tasks are to care for the farm animals, but also to build a permaculture garden, outdoor area and greenhouse around the volunteer base. There are many learning opportunities: from how to create your own garden, to understanding more about eco-sustainability, the GEN network, writing European Solidarity Corps applications, etc. Volunteers will be involved daily in Charlottendals farm where they will live, but also have the opportunity to connect with other permaculture farms and gardens such as Nibble Gård in Järna. There is also an interesting education we can interact with called the YIP, Youth Initiative Program, https://yip.se/   Järna has been called an "alternative capital" 

Please be aware that we are currently organizing the interviewing process thus it can take up the a few for us to respond.

All accommodation, food and travel expenses are covered. 
The volunteers will live in their own house in the Eco village. Each participant will have their own bedroom and they will share a common area (kitchen, bathroom). The volunteers will have a card with the monthly food allowance and will grow food. The food is ecological, healthy and vegetarian. During workdays the volunteers will prepare and have lunch together.
The travel reimbursement will be calculated based on travel distance and type of travel. We encourage green travel when possible. Each volunteer will have access to a bike.

Training during the activity
On arrival the participants will be welcomed by their coordinators and mentors, involving members of the community and past ESC volunteers. They will be given an introduction to safety measures, a tour of the town and Ecovillage and have a selection of books and documentaries at their disposal. The volunteers will take part in an On-Arrival Training Course and a Mid-Term Training Course in Stockholm, held by the Swedish National Agency (MUCF).

The volunteers we are looking for will be living on a farm in Sweden, near Stockholm. involved activities on animal and environmental care, that is acting locally on global issues and up to carry out tasks that involve getting your hands dirty! We would prefer a candidate who has a minimum of experience working with gardening, building and animal care and interest in permaculture. Other tasks include youth leadership, promotion and administration. Please also note that weather and darkness during low season is a big factor in Sweden, especially if you come from a warm country.
To apply, please send CV and a motivational letter to evs.charlottendal@gmail.com. If possible also specify the desired duration as well as starting date of the volunteering.

Los voluntarios participarán en un proyecto de recuperación de bosques mediterráneos en tierras desertificadas por la larga tradición de la agricultura y la ganadería. Los jóvenes aprenderán el papel fundamental que tienen los bosques en nuestros ecosistemas y nociones básicas sobre la recuperación de suelos desertificados. Podrán experimentar la restauración de ecosistemas desde su planteamiento hasta su ejecución. Las actividades incluyen la recuperación de charcas, la instalación de refugios para aves y pequeños mamíferos, plantación de arbustos, árboles y todo lo relacionado con la buena recuperación de un entorno. En esta actividad habrá constante supervisión del responsable de los voluntariados y del técnico del proyecto.

Se ofrecen diversos alojamientos para hospedar a los participantes, están completamente equipados y cuentan con todo el menaje necesario. Cada uno tiene habitaciones compartidas para 2 personas y zonas comunes (baño y cocina), además de una zona de piscina disponible durante los meses de verano. Todos los participantes recibirán una asignación de manutención. La fundación está situada a 5 minutos en bicicleta del pueblo El Álamo. Este pueblo cuenta con todas las instalaciones y establecimientos necesarios y transporte público a Madrid.

Esta actividad capacita a jóvenes en reforestación y restauración de ecosistemas, enseñándoles el proceso de mejora de la biodiversidad en zonas áridas. Adquirirán conocimientos sobre impermeabilización y restauración de charcas para cría de anfibios, técnicas sostenibles de plantación, seguimiento de fauna por fototrampeo y fabricación de refugios para animales. La formación incluye teoría y práctica, material didáctico, una charla introductoria y seminarios sobre proyectos del centro. La práctica especializada implica realizar tareas diarias bajo supervisión del responsable.

El perfil ideal para un participante en el voluntariado europeo en el proyecto de Restauración ecológica incluye ciertos requisitos generales y competencias específicas. Los participantes deben tener entre 20 y 30 años y conocimientos de español medio-alto para comunicarse de manera efectiva en el día a día. Es esencial que puedan comprometerse a participar durante 13 semanas aproximadamente. Se valora experiencia previa en proyectos ambientales o voluntariados similares. El candidato debe tener una pasión por la conservación del medio ambiente, interés en la reforestación y restauración de ecosistemas, y motivación para aprender sobre técnicas de sostenibilidad y biodiversidad.
Es fundamental que el participante tenga la capacidad de trabajar en equipo y adaptarse a entornos multiculturales, además de contar con buena condición física para realizar tareas al aire libre en las diferentes épocas del año. Las habilidades de comunicación y la capacidad para seguir instrucciones son igualmente importantes.
El compromiso incluye la disponibilidad para participar durante el período completo del proyecto, una actitud proactiva y disposición para trabajar en condiciones variables. También se requiere flexibilidad y disposición para realizar diversas tareas relacionadas con el proyecto. 
Esta es una oportunidad de adquirir conocimientos prácticos y teóricos en restauración ecológica y a su vez de desarrollar habilidades personales y profesionales de una forma enriquecedora en un entorno internacional y colaborativo. Por tanto, lo más esencial es la disposición, el compromiso y ganas de disfrutar la experiencia.

In this placement you will gain insights into a diverse ecological and sustainable agriculture. We grow 30 different types of vegetables, care for and milk 60 dairy goats, make our own cheese and run a plastic-free farm shop. Our products are also used to cook lunch for the community. So your tasks in this placement are very diverse. You will grow and harvest vegetables, take care of and milk the goats, make cheese and help out in the farm shop. After an introduction and some practical experience in all areas, you can choose your own focus of work, depending on your interests, and you can also implement your own ideas, such as building climbing elements for the goats or creating new types of cheese. If you like working outdoors, being in contact with animals and people and enjoy processing products, Blumenthal is the right place for you!

We eat organic and vegetarian food. As a volunteer you have your own room in a shared apartment with other volunteers. You share the combined kitchen and living room as well as the bathroom. You can also use the common room, the large garden and park. We have a car sharing, where you can become a member (depending on your license). And there is a “dance room”, meditation space and a sauna that can be used by everyone.
Covered during ESC: Free food and accommodation, health insurance, pocket money.

The community has a lot of events and rituals; we welcome you to join them and get to know the people living with you. Dancing together and spending time around the campfire, practising yoga and mediation or playing board games are opportunities to participate in community life. 
We also celebrate traditional holidays like Easter and have community events for many other occasions. There are regular concerts, festivals and courses in Blumenthal, to which you are cordially invited.

Furthermore you'll attend two mandatory trainings organised by the ESC programme.

We're looking for participants who have...
• Interest in sustainability and community living, in a rural location.
• Openness to learn and meet new people.
• Motivation to work in the community and on a farm.
• English or German language skills (German language skills are welcome but not a requirement if you speak English).
• Willingness to learn German or improve your German language skills 
and are happy to work 30 hours per week. 

If you are interested in applying, please fill in the online survey: https://forms.gle/kYaTQEyAdrP7x2Jr9
Read more about the application process and the deadline: schloss-blumenthal.de/biohof
Questions? Please contact Kathrin Schaefer, our volunteer coordinator for ESC: volunteers@schloss-blumenthal.de

Alianza por la Solidaridad, a member of ActionAid, aims to achieve active citizenship that fights against inequalities and for the recognition of human rights. The volunteer will take part in cooperation and humanitarian aid projects, supporting monitoring and evaluation activities across the organization’s initiatives. They will help ensure compliance with organizational policies and tools, contribute to the design of monitoring systems, and assist in collecting and analyzing information to track project indicators and prepare reports. The volunteer will also support the development of strategies and guidelines for monitoring, evaluation, and accountability within national-level projects. The position is full-time, Monday to Friday, and includes occasional field visits.

You will have the opportunity to live in a house with a private room, access to shared services, Wi-Fi, a mobile communication card, and the residence is close to the office with convenient access to local transportation. You will receive a monthly allowance of 607,98€ for your personal expenses, including food and local transport. You will also be able to interact with the communities where we carry out our projects.

You will receive training covering topics such as an introduction to Alianza por la Solidaridad and the European Solidarity Corps, the rights and responsibilities of both the organization and the volunteer, Youthpass, Henner insurance, and SHEA. In addition, you will learn about the management and implementation of monitoring and evaluation activities in humanitarian and development NGOs, expanding your knowledge of reporting procedures, best practices, guidelines, and tools with a special focus on impact evaluation.

We are looking for a volunteer who is eager to learn, work collaboratively within a team, and adapt to the local context. An interest in project monitoring and follow-up activities in cooperation projects is essential; studies or experience in monitoring and evaluation will be considered an asset. A minimum of an elementary level of Spanish is required. This volunteering opportunity is open to everyone. Whether you are a migrant, live in a rural area, have limited economic resources, or face other challenges don’t hesitate to apply! This experience is designed to be inclusive, accessible, and empowering for all.

The "Learning through play" program is a unique opportunity for young people with an interest or experience in the humanitarian sector, education, or youth support. Volunteers promote social inclusion, solidarity, and resilience through activities that develop skills, boost self-confidence, and cultivate personal expression and empowerment. 
They will participate in experiential English language lessons, creative workshops, artistic activities, and sports activities, while 
•    taking an active role in Street Work activities through the Mobile School mobile educational unit. 
•	promote the development of volunteering through research and awareness-raising activities, which will include approaching, informing, and activating new volunteers
•    research activities examining contemporary trends and challenges in volunteering, offering a comprehensive experience that combines practical support with an analytical understanding of volunteering today.

For volunteers coming from outside Thessaloniki, accommodation is provided in fully equipped apartments with roommates, located close to public transportation. In addition, regardless of their place of origin, volunteers will receive a monthly allowance of €210 as pocket money, €150 for food, and a monthly unlimited travel card for Thessaloniki's public transport (buses and metro).
The minimum duration of the program is 45 days with 30 hours of work per week, and it takes place at the ARSIS Youth Support Center at 9 Spartis Street.

Participants will receive training in key areas of the program, such as:
•    Mobile School Methodology: Specialized techniques for using the mobile educational structure.
•    Teaching English: Guidelines for adapting lessons to different levels and needs.
•    Youth Empowerment: Approaches to supporting vulnerable groups and creating inclusive environments.
•    Action research methodology and public awareness of volunteering.
ARSIS provides ongoing support and guidance throughout the activity, ensuring that volunteers feel confident and prepared for their role.

We are looking for young people aged 18-30 from Bulgaria, Turkey, North Macedonia, or Spain, with a background or studies in education, psychosocial support, youth support, or the humanitarian sector. Experience in voluntary activities and familiarity with non-formal education approaches are desirable, while the ability to work in a team, empathy, and a genuine desire to contribute to society are essential.

The Uganda Pioneers’ Association (UPA) is a youth-led NGO dedicated to community development, intercultural cooperation, and youth empowerment across Uganda. As a volunteer, you will support UPA by facilitating knowledge sharing and capacity building among staff through trainings on digital skills, communication, and social media marketing strategies. You will also assist in managing and upgrading UPA’s digital platforms to enhance online engagement. In addition, the role includes providing ICT training for UPA staff and local partner organizations, such as schools and community-based groups, helping teams strengthen their digital communication and marketing skills. These efforts empower UPA and its partners to effectively leverage technology for outreach, education, and community development.

Volunteers will stay at Villa Mamu, Mengo, Kampala, a spacious residence with WiFi, a warm shower, a kitchen, and pets. For a deeper cultural experience, some days will be spent with a host family near Kikooba School. Other accommodation options in Kampala can be arranged based on safety and convenience.
Local transport mainly consists of boda-bodas (motorcycle taxis). Traveling to Kampala city takes about two hours by public transport at approximately 10,000 UGX one way. This setup offers a comfortable and exciting experience, blending urban amenities with meaningful community engagement.

As part of the BRIDGE Project (Building Resilience, Innovation, Development, and Gender Equality), volunteers will work toward empowering vulnerable communities, especially women. Training includes skills development workshops, digital literacy enhancement, participation in UN Women Summits, and facilitating digital training sessions. Volunteers will gain hands-on experience in capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and social impact-driven project execution while refining leadership and communication skills. Visit: https://mondo.org.ee/en/volunteers/

The volunteer should have a strong interest in digital technology, communication, and marketing, with a particular passion for social media and teaching. They should demonstrate creativity and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to work flexibly and collaboratively in a team environment with enthusiasm and commitment. Over AAP
Wij zijn een Europese dierenwelzijnsorganisatie die zich inzet voor het welzijn van exotische dieren. Het is onze missie om een einde te maken aan hun lijden door dieren in nood te redden en te pleiten voor betere wet- en regelgeving. De dieren die bij AAP terechtkomen, zijn vaak afkomstig uit de illegale handel, circussen, illegale dierentuinen of rechtstreeks van particulieren.


Jouw rol
Je komt te werken onder begeleiding van een ervaren dierverzorger en zal je voornamelijk bezighouden met schoonmaken van de verblijven (dit is 70% van het werk). Hiernaast maak je verrijking voor de dieren en help je met het inrichten van de verblijven.

Hier woon je niet alleen samen met andere ESC-vrijwilligers, maar ook met vrijwilligers die bij AAP werken. Maandelijks krijg je voedsel- en zakgeld en op werkdagen krijg je gratis lunch. full_description:
In connection with the European project coordinator, the territorial coordinator of a FEDER-funded project on ecological and social transitions, and the teams of several local social centers, the volunteer will take part in a collective initiative addressing key challenges such as sustainable mobility, responsible consumption, recycling, digital inclusion, and energy transition. Through workshops, events and daily interactions with local residents, the volunteer will be encouraged to share ideas and practices from their own country, co-create solutions with the community, and contribute to raising awareness on these issues. They will also participate in coordination meetings with other centers, promote European mobility opportunities among local youth, and take part in intercultural activities to share their culture and experience.

The volunteer will be selected for this mission. He/she will share a two-bedroom apartment. It is located in the town center of Saint-Martin-Boulogne near shops and public transports. The volunteers will receive an allowance of 400€ for food, and pocket money. Bellidée will provide a bus card (for transport in the Communauté d'Agglomération du Boulonnais) and a train card (for transport in the Hauts-de-France region). They will also have free access to all the services of Bellidée (sports, cultural events, etc.).

The volunteer will have to assist to the two training sessions organized by the French National Agency. She/He will also be able to participate to trainings organized by the Bellidée. The volunteer will have access to the EU Academy platform and will have courses with a volunteer to help her/him to learn French.

We are looking for someone curious, motivated and willing to engage with local communities on ecological and social topics. The volunteer should be open-minded, proactive, and eager to share ideas and practices from their own culture, while co-creating solutions with others. A strong interest in sustainability, community work, or European values is welcome. The ability to work both independently and in a team will be essential, as the volunteer will take part in collective actions and local events with various partners.

Fondazione Don Giovanni Zanandrea  was founded in 1918 in Cento, a  little municipality in Emilia Romagna to answer the most urgent needs of the fragile population. Since 1984 ZANANDREA has been working in the field of disability.  The main activities include: Pilacà: a day center which assists people with cognitive, physical and psychiatric disabilities through an educational/assistance approach, provides health care and pedagogical/psychological support. Through Non-Formal educational activities, promotes the acquisition/maintenance of autonomy. - CSO: a protected laboratory that aims to facilitate the insertion into the labor market of peolple with disability. - Freed-Home: a project about independent living for young people with low-support needs disability. During the year ZANANDREA promotes other projects like work placement/training/orientation, activities for young autistic people, baskin (inclusive basket), public fundraising events with music, food and drinks and movienights.

As with other volunteer projects, travel expenses are reimbursed up to a ceiling set by the European Commission. Food, accommodation, language course, training, mentoring/tutoring, monthly pocket money and insurance are covered by the host organization. Fondazione Zanandrea is located in the historic center of the city of Cento. The apartment as well as all the activities are within walking distance, but volunteers will still be offered a bicycle to use for their own journeys. A few hundred meters away is the Cento bus station with connections to Bologna, Modena and Ferrara.

Playful-recreational workshops and ateliers alongside operators and educators to ensure growth, empowerment and the maintenance of individual autonomy acquired by users . Volunteers will be able to collaborate in all the main and side projects and activities like Music therapy, sports tournaments, dance and relaxation, excursions in the area, artistic workshops, multimedia activities and any non-formal stimulus that the volunteers will want to bring as personal baggage. Motivation and willingness to work with people with disabilities;  Good communication skills; Motivation to learn; Contribute by bringing your personal skills like skills in the field of music, sports, art, theatre, manual and multimedia activities, etc.

The VALE Association is offering two long-term individual volunteer positions for a period of 12 months. Our organisation is a reference at regional and provincial level in the field of people with disabilities. The tasks to be developed during the volunteering project will be mainly the support of the activities carried out by the entity, as well as the organisation of workshops for the users of the day centre.

200 euros will be provided for food money, as well as 6 euros per day as pocket money. Travel costs (by public transport) will also be covered within a budget band to be determined according to the distance between the home country and Spain.  Accommodation will be in a room with other volunteers, sharing a room with another volunteer of the same gender.

During the volunteering project, participants will receive a follow-up of the tasks they carry out, as well as training specifically in the field of inclusion and disability.

We are looking for a person with previous experience in social work, and work in the field of inclusion or related to people with disabilities will be an asset. An intermediate level of English is required and a basic level of Spanish would be an asset.

"Arabkir" Medical Center stands as the largest pediatric facility in Armenia, dedicated to providing comprehensive medical services encompassing prevention, diagnostics, and treatment of various childhood deceases. 
The primary objective of the project is to engage with hospitalized children at "Arabkir" Medical Center.
Volunteer responsibilities include:
• Assisting children in arts workshops and supporting staff in organizing activities such as painting and sculpting.
• Facilitating basic foreign language classes.
• Showcasing their cultural heritage through dance, musical events, and teaching traditional songs.
• Conducting workshops on diverse topics of interest.
• Organizing approved excursions, outdoor activities, as well as sports events, themed evenings, and meetings.
This project is conducted with the support of the Voluntary Service of Armenia HUJ and spans a duration of 8-12 months.

The volunteers will be provided with convenient accommodation: the dormitory of a university in Yerevan, near the city center, featuring same-gendered rooms with two occupants each, shared bathroom, and a spacious kitchen. This cozy dormitory is equipped with all necessities and ensures safety. Approximately 19 long-term HUJ volunteers from different European countries reside in the dormitory. On the first of each month, volunteers receive a monthly allowance, sent by HUJ to their bank cards, covering their pocket money, food, transportation, and internet expenses.

Upon the volunteer's arrival at the airport, they will receive a warm welcome by HUJ. Following this, an introductory meeting will be held at the HUJ office, where the organizational staff will formally greet the volunteers and assist in essential procedures for their stay in Yerevan (obtaining an Armenian phone number, a physical bank card, and arranging a meeting with their assigned mentor). During their mobility in Yerevan, volunteers will engage in two training sessions - an on-arrival and a mid-term training - organized by SALTO in Georgia.

There are no gender restrictions regarding the selection/recruitment of volunteers. As per the ESC guide, the age of the volunteer should range from 18-30. The volunteer should be interested or have some experience in working with children; he/she should be enthusiastic, responsible, respectful, thoughtful and reliable. The main criterion for the choice of the volunteer-to-be are the activities they have planned for the project.

Verbund Sozialer Dienste (VSD) operates in the field of child and youth welfare in the area surrounding Bad Essen, near Osnabrück. Its subsidiary, Dialog, manages decentralized in-patient residential groups within the German child and youth service system. Volunteers contribute by sharing aspects of their own cultural backgrounds, fostering openness and understanding of other cultures and ethnic groups. This cultural exchange adds variety to daily life and promotes tolerance within the community.

We prioritize the well-being of our volunteers and offer comprehensive support and guidance before, during, and after the project. Ensuring you feel comfortable and valued is important to us, which is why we have established a well-structured support system. We respect individual dietary preferences, carefully consider food intolerances, and take proactive steps to meet your needs. Meals are provided at the workplace, and the full meal allowance will be paid in full. Transportation costs will be reimbursed upon submission of proof of purchase.

To further enhance the experience, we also offer opportunities for personal and professional development, including workshops, skill-building sessions, and guidance on navigating the local culture and administrative systems. Volunteers can participate in networking events to connect with local organizations and other volunteers, fostering collaboration and exchange. Additionally, we provide ongoing feedback and support to ensure that volunteers not only succeed in their roles but also gain valuable insights and skills for their future endeavors.

The participants should be socially engaged and open to new experiences, with a genuine willingness to work with disadvantaged children. Prior knowledge in social work or psychology is an advantage. Ideally, volunteers should be able to remain composed in crisis situations. It is expected that volunteers approach training and learning opportunities provided by the hosting organization to handle crises with an open mindset, while maintaining a strong commitment to staying connected with the children. Additionally, volunteers are encouraged to share aspects of their own culture with the children, fostering cultural exchange.

DIVE25 is a European Solidarity Corps project hosted by Adamastor in Viseu, Portugal, designed to empower young people through a dynamic blend of digital inclusion, civic engagement, environmental action, and cultural diversity. The project runs throughout 2025 and brings together local and international volunteers committed to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and participatory Europe.

Guided by the EU Youth Goals, DIVE25 responds to today’s most pressing challenges—social inequality, climate change, and digital exclusion—by creating opportunities for young people to act, learn, and lead in their communities. Accommodation for volunteers is available at the Viseu Youth Hostel, providing a comfortable and social environment for participants. At the beginning of each month, volunteers receive an allocated amount for food expenses, as determined by the European Solidarity Corps program. This enables them to manage their own meals throughout the month. In addition to accommodation and food, the program covers travel expenses, including round-trip transportation, allowing participants to fully focus on their roles without financial worries.

During DIVE25, volunteers receive on-arrival training covering ESC, Youthpass, Portuguese culture, and team-building. Ongoing mentoring supports personal growth, with regular reflection sessions and a mid-term evaluation. At the end, volunteers complete a Youthpass process to recognize and document their learning outcomes for future opportunities.

The ideal volunteer for the Dive25 project is a motivated young person aged between 18 and 30, eager to engage in social and community-based activities. They should be open-minded, adaptable, and passionate about solidarity, inclusion, and cultural exchange. A strong interest in personal development, gaining new experiences, and becoming an active agent of change is essential. Additionally, the volunteer should be flexible, empathetic, and ready to work in a diverse, multicultural environment, collaborating with people from different backgrounds. An interest in local culture and European solidarity is a plus.

Would you like to welcome a volunteer for SEO/BirdLife, meeting people of all over Europe, and being part of our nature conservation team? Riet Vell Nature Reserve right in the middle of Ebro Delta has a wide variety of opportunities which you can get involved in, with something to suit everyone. The volunteer role here at Riet Vell are mostly practical conservation-based ones with opportunities to get involved in environmental education, flora and fauna surveys and public events. Volunteering can be flexible around you. You will get to meet new people and learn new skills in a beautiful wetland setting. What you can expect? Habitat management, bird surveys, beach cleans, site patrols, general repairs, site access maintenance, events, fixed point photography, mapping of invasive species, butterfly surveys, bird and bat boxes checks, bird ringing campaigns. Speed up your Spanish learning through supporting with customer service for our public at Riet Vell Nature Reserve Visitor Centre.

The volunteer will live in the Home of the Volunteers located in the Riet Vell Nature Reserve.  The house is a partially renovated old house that meets the basic requirements, with two bathrooms, one toilet, shared kitchen and dining room, all basic accessories, including washing machine, basic furniture, computer office, living room and four shared bedrooms. WiFi is free both at the house and the visitor Center. You will have access to a vehicle that can be used out of volunteer activity time. Finacial support amount of 330 € per month that covers food and pocket money availability.

The work of the volunteers will have as their final objective their training as professionals linked to nature and the environment learning about monitoring and management techniques, as well as other basic skills needed in an natural, agricultural and rural environment. There will be different types of tasks available and volunteers will be able to choose which task best suits their skills and which ones they can help them develop new skills. Part of the activities will be demonstrative, such as workshops and field trips with other environmental management organisations.

A more scientific profile is preferably sought and / or related to the environment (because many of the tasks have a scientific and conservation character). When this need is covered, the horizon opens in looking for people with other varied profiles with or without higher education, in order to have a multidisciplinary team because it refers to the interests and abilities of each volunteer. Also volunteers with good communication skill are welcome to work in our visitor center and to manage the Reserve social networks.

full_description:
Malagne Archéoparc is a non-profit organisation managing a Gallo-roman archaeological site. Its aims are to enhance and protect the heritages, to pass on and share knowledges about Gallo-roman history through know-hows and techniques, to make the past alive through scientific researches based on experimental archaeology, through animals living on site... and rediscovering of old techniques. The volunteers' (2) tasks will be to help in mostly manual tasks: gardening, fixing fences, pruning, building shelters and bridgefoot, taking care of the animals to help the team in the maintenance of the archeological site. To a lesser extent, volunteers can be involved in pedagogical tasks: helping the pedagogical staff with groups of children visiting, supporting during the re-enactement event, showing how to bake bread, forge with traditional techniques. Busy period from April until October.

The volunteers will have a private room in a fully-equipped shared house in the city of Rochefort with other ESC volunteers (1.5 km away from the Archéoparc). Food: the volunteer will receive a budget and will take care of the meals by themself. Participation in the ESC is free of charge for the participant, except for exceptional contribution to travel costs. The volunteer will receive free board and lodging during the whole activity. In addition, they will receive a small allowance (pocket money) for personal expenses throughout the duration of the activity.

With the French-speaking National Agency of Belgium: on-arrival and mid-term seminars. With the support organization in Belgium (Association des Compagnons Bâtisseurs asbl, "CBB"): residential weekends and networking activities with other ESC volunteers on other projects supported by CBB in the French-speaking part of Belgium. The volunteers should be ready to take an active part in the collective networking activities and can count on many local resources to create personal projects. French classes available

TO APPLY CHECK THIS LINK AND FILL IN THE FORM IN THE TAB "REGISTER" : https://compagnonsbatisseurs.world/activities/long-term/esc-volunteering/malagne/ The volunteers must be motivated to join the activity; open-minded and pro-active; agreeing with a very flexible schedule throughout the year; not be afraid of spending time outside and to appreciate the contact with nature; certificate of good conduct. It is also important not to have allergies or fear for animals.

6 months voluntarism opportunity starting in October, aimsing to support unaccompanied asylum seeker minors' well-being and education, and to raise awareness about asylum seeker theme among the local citizens. Main activities of a volunteer are going to be planning, preparation and implementation of informal and non-formal educational activities for male asylum seeker teenagers in ages 14-17, as well as work on online content creation (articles, photography, video, podcasts, research, etc) on themes related to asylum seekers. Each volunteer will implement non-formal education activities with teenagers 3-5 times a week, attend weekly preparation meetings 2 times a week and work on online content creation project (on themes connecting with asylum seeker integration) few hours every day.

Accommodation will be in apartment in the city center (shared bedroom with 1 or 2 other volunteers of the same gender), 2 minutes walking distance from the office. The apartment includes several bedrooms, shared kitchen and living room, bathroom and a big balcony. It also includes wifi, basic appliances and items.
The volunteer will monthly receive 7 Euros a day for food expenses, as well as pocket money 7 Euros a day, prepaid each month. Transportation will be provided (car with a driver/sometimes bus) for activities that will take place in the asylum seeker accommodation facility.

Volunteers will be trained to follow the organisation's Code of Conduct and specific rules of their work field. During the integration days, volunteers will receive training and/or information about safety, protection and security, specifically child protection, hygiene and health, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse, and non-formal education in the context of unaccompanied asylum seeker integration. Additionally, support for working with digital tools will be provided when needed. Volunteers will also receive weekly and monthly monitoring and support during meetings.

We are looking for applicants aged 22 - 30, fluent in English, independent, eager to research and regularly propose / initiate activities, work in an international team, be responsible and comply with our rules and regulations with a very high sense of responsibility, creative and flexible. EXPERIENCE IS REQUESTED in at least in one of the areas: studies in social sciences / work or volunteering with young people in the area of non-formal education or similar / work or volunteering with young asylum seekers/refugees. Video making and other type of content creation experience will be considered as a strong asset for the applicants.

This short term volunteering placement will have Employment and Education themes but with priorities linked to addressing the issue of inclusion and diversity as a societal challenge

Supporting the Youth Work Team in Mullingar, you will gain solid experience as a youth and community support across a range of activities in a busy hub in central Mullingar.

Aimed at local young people aged 18+ who reside in the local area to give priority access to this opportunity.
Bikes can be provided to support with transport, and any other challenges with access will be taken under consideration.

Food / Refreshments are availabe for all our staff and young people, our volunteers will be included as part of the team.

Pocket money and food allowance will be offered and outlined in the Volunteering agreement.

Advanced planning visits and training is provided for all our volunteers.  Those who require accompanying persons will be fully supported.  Here you will meet your mentors and other solidarity corps volunteers.

We have an in depth induction programme so you will be fully aware of the organisation, the project and your role
Daily shadowing, coaching and support will be on offer.

We are looking for someone who is eager to learn, help others and offer their own skills and talents in the spirit of Solidarity.
Ages 18+ from the local area and knowledge of the youth projects and their purpose.

Any skills or talents in the area of Drama, Music, Sport, Art, Digital / Technology / Outdoors would be great - but bring your own magic to our project.

For 30 years, EHO has worked to create a fairer society, emphasizing human dignity, philanthropy, equality, and social justice for all. As an Education Assistant in the "Poverty to Power" program, you will provide educational and psychosocial support and interventions to empower children facing social exclusion, poverty, forced marriages, violence, abuse, and deprivation. Your role includes facilitating creative workshops using non-formal educational methods (arts, crafts, drawing, puppetry, and language learning). You'll also offer one-on-one support for children's learning and homework, fostering positive, respectful relationships. Collaborating with other volunteers and staff, you'll help tailor the program to meet the diverse needs of the children. Additionally, you'll monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of the program to ensure children improvements. Your cooperation with the Center for Social Care and Center for Migrants will further enhance the project's impact and outreach.

You will be accommodated in a spacious apartment in Novi Sad, with each volunteer enjoying their own private room. The apartment will have at least three bedrooms, along with a shared bathroom and a fully equipped kitchen. All necessary furniture will be provided.
